boundaries.evidence: The index set I is nonempty for every e>=2 and step 3.2 records this explicitly; steps 1.3 and 3.1 evaluate the sums of alpha_i and of the h_i over the full nonempty index set, so no empty-sum convention is left tacit.

The kernel vector is used rather than divided by: step 2.1 compares delta-coefficients to get x_0=0 and then uses the kernel direction (1,...,1) of A, the vector (1,1) at e=2, while step 1.3 proves both row sums vanish.

boundaries.reason: The only normalization constant is the symmetrizer entry d_i=1 fixed in the Definition; no singleton cardinality, empty product or unit-coefficient convention enters the Verification, which works with the explicitly chosen bases.

boundaries.evidence: The degenerate boundary e=2 is treated as its own case: step 1.1 checks the double-edge matrix against the GCM axioms, step 2.1 uses the kernel direction (1,1), and step 3.3 verifies the reflection exchanging Lambda_0 and Lambda_1.

The affine end label is exactly i=0: step 2.1 compares the delta-coefficient to isolate x_0, step 2.2 computes the d-pairing equal to delta_{i0} at that label, and step 4.1 defines the root form on the splitting with the Lambda_0 factor.

Both lattices come with explicit chosen bases, the Lambda_i together with delta and the h_i together with d, and steps 1.2 through 4.1 verify properties of those fixed bases; nothing is selected from an infinite family, so no choice principle is invoked.

boundaries.reason: The Statement is a list of identities and structural claims about one fixed datum; it contains no if-and-only-if assertion, so there is no forward direction of a biconditional to discharge.
No converse implication is asserted: independence of the roots, the row sums, the pairings and tau-invariance are each verified directly in the numbered steps, so no reverse direction is owed.

citations.quote: A **generalized Cartan matrix** (GCM) is an integer matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$, where $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $n\ge1$, such that $a_{ii}=2$, $a_{ij}\le0$ for $i\ne j$, and $a_{ij}=0\iff a_{ji}=0$. It is **indecomposable** if there is no partition $I=J\sqcup K$ into nonempty sets with all entries between $J$ and $K$ zero.

A GCM $A$ is **symmetrizable** if there is a diagonal matrix $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with real $d_i>0$ such that $B=DA$ is symmetric, equivalently $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$. We fix one such $D$ when using a form.

The convention for GCM is [[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]]. One may take the $d_i$ positive rational, or positive integer after scaling. Indeed, in each connected component of the nonzero-entry graph, fix its least index $v$ and replace $d_i$ by $d_i/d_v$. Along an edge $ij$, $d_j/d_i=a_{ij}/a_{ji}$ is positive rational. A finite path from $v$ to $i$ therefore gives rational $d_i/d_v$; its value is independent of the path because the original real symmetrizer supplies the same ratio. Multiplication by the finite product of denominators gives integers. Isolated vertices are assigned 1. Kleshchev writes $A=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon_i)B$; our convention has $d_i=\varepsilon_i^{-1}$.

A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.

A **minimal realization** of a GCM $A$ of rank $r$ is a complex vector space $\mathfrak h$ with indexed linearly independent families $h_1,\ldots,h_n\in\mathfrak h$ and $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n\in\mathfrak h^*$ such that $\alpha_j(h_i)=a_{ij}$ and $\dim\mathfrak h=2n-r$. An isomorphism $T$ of realizations satisfies $T(h_i)=h_i^\prime$ and $\alpha_j^\prime T=\alpha_j$ for every index.

The matrix convention is [[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]]. Existence and uniqueness up to isomorphism are supplied by [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]. Uniqueness of the isomorphism is not asserted.

For a realization as in [[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], set $Q=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ and $Q^+=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Define $\operatorname{ht}(\sum_i k_i\alpha_i)=\sum_i k_i$. For $\lambda,\mu\in\mathfrak h^*$ write $\mu\le\lambda$ if $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$.

Independence of the simple roots makes coordinates unique. Thus $Q^+\cap(-Q^+)=\{0\}$, which proves antisymmetry of the order; closure under addition proves transitivity, and $0\in Q^+$ proves reflexivity. Positive roots will belong to $Q^+\setminus\{0\}$, not all of $Q^+$.

Fix a minimal realization $(\mathfrak h,(h_i),(\alpha_i))$ of a finite GCM $A$, with the row-coroot convention $\alpha_j(h_i)=a_{ij}$ from [[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]]. Define

$$P=\{\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*: \lambda(h_i)\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }i\},\qquad P^+=\{\lambda\in P:\lambda(h_i)\geq0\text{ for every }i\}.$$

Elements of $P$ are **integral weights**; elements of $P^+$ are **dominant integral weights**. Their simple-coroot labels are the integers $\lambda(h_i)$. Zero labels are allowed, and the zero functional is dominant integral.

The independent coroots can be extended to a finite basis of $\mathfrak h$. Prescribing integral labels on the coroots and arbitrary complex values on the remaining basis vectors specifies a unique functional. Thus complementary Cartan values are unrestricted; $P$ need not be a discrete lattice in $\mathfrak h^*$. The inequalities only concern the integral coroot labels, not an ordering of arbitrary complex Cartan values. This definition uses finite linear algebra and no AC.

derivations.claim: $A$ is a generalized Cartan matrix. By construction $a_{ii}=2$ and $a_{ij}\le0$ for $i\ne j$; off-diagonal entries vanish except for the neighbouring entries $-1$ and, at $e=2$, the double edge $-2$, and $A$ is symmetric, so $a_{ij}=0\iff a_{ji}=0$. Hence [F1] applies, $D=\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1)$ is a symmetrizer, and $A$ is symmetrizable.

The pairing is perfect on the displayed bases. The families $\{\Lambda_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{\delta\}$ and $\{h_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{d\}$ are bases of the free abelian groups $P$ and $P^\vee$, and the four displayed rules give $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ on all basis pairs as the identity matrix. Hence every homomorphism $P\to\mathbb Z$ is $\langle\cdot,\xi\rangle$ for a unique $\xi\in P^\vee$, and in particular the simple coroots are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$.
The row and column sums of $A$ vanish: $\sum_{j\in I}a_{ij}=0=\sum_{j\in I}a_{ji}$ for every $i\in I$, by [F7] and symmetry of $A$.

The simple roots are linearly independent. Let $\sum_i x_i\alpha_i=0$ with $x_i\in\mathbb Z$. Comparing coefficients of $\delta$ in $\alpha_i=\sum_j a_{ji}\Lambda_j+\delta_{i0}\delta$ gives $x_0=0$, and comparing coefficients of $\Lambda_k$ gives $\sum_i x_i a_{ki}=0$ for every $k$. For $e\ge3$ this reads $2x_k-x_{k+1}-x_{k-1}=0$, so all differences $x_{k+1}-x_k$ are equal; their sum over the cycle $I$ is $0$, so each difference is $0$ and $x$ is constant, and $x_0=0$ forces $x=0$. For $e=2$ the two equations $2x_0-2x_1=0$ and $2x_1-2x_0=0$ together with $x_0=0$ give $x_1=0$. Hence the $\alpha_i$ are independent and freely generate $Q$.

The simple-root identities of the datum hold: $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=\sum_k a_{kj}\langle\Lambda_k,h_i\rangle+\delta_{j0}\langle\delta,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$; $\langle\alpha_i,d\rangle=\sum_k a_{ki}\langle\Lambda_k,d\rangle+\delta_{i0}\langle\delta,d\rangle=\delta_{i0}$; and $\sum_{i\in I}\alpha_i=\sum_k\bigl(\sum_i a_{ki}\bigr)\Lambda_k+\delta=\delta$, because every column sum of $A$ vanishes by step 1.3. In particular $\alpha_i\in P$ and its coordinates in the basis of $P$ are the displayed integers.

The level functional and the central element are as claimed. By step 1.2 the rules $\langle c,\Lambda_i\rangle=1$ and $\langle c,\delta\rangle=0$ define a homomorphism $P\to\mathbb Z$, the level; and $\langle c,\alpha_j\rangle=\sum_i\langle h_i,\alpha_j\rangle=\sum_i a_{ij}=0$ for every $j$ by step 1.3, so all simple roots, hence all of $Q$, have level $0$. Every $\lambda\in P$ has integral labels $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$ on the coroots by the displayed rules, so $P$ meets the integral-weight conditions of [F5] on $P^\vee$.

The datum $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee)$ is a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group. The index set is finite and nonempty; $A$ is a symmetrizable GCM with symmetrizer $D$ by step 1.1; $P$ and $P^\vee$ are free abelian groups with an integer pairing, perfect on the displayed bases, by step 1.2; the simple coroots are independent by step 1.2; and the simple roots are independent, generate the root lattice freely, and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ by steps 2.1 and 2.2. Hence [F2] and the realization axioms of [F3] hold, the rank is $e+1$, and $q_i=q$ for all $i$.

The diagram reflection $\tau$ is a well-defined involution preserving the pairing and the root data. It permutes the basis $\{\Lambda_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{\delta\}$ and the basis $\{h_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{d\}$, so it is an automorphism of $P$ and of $P^\vee$ with $\tau^2=\operatorname{id}$. On basis pairs, $\langle\tau\Lambda_j,\tau h_i\rangle=\langle\Lambda_{-j},h_{-i}\rangle=\delta_{-j,-i}=\delta_{ij}=\langle\Lambda_j,h_i\rangle$, while $\langle\tau\delta,\tau h_i\rangle=0$, $\langle\tau\Lambda_j,\tau d\rangle=0$ and $\langle\tau\delta,\tau d\rangle=1$, so the pairing is preserved. Finally $\tau(\alpha_i)=\sum_j a_{ji}\Lambda_{-j}+\delta_{i0}\delta=\sum_k a_{-k,i}\Lambda_k+\delta_{i0}\delta=\alpha_{-i}$, because $a_{-k,i}=a_{k,-i}$ holds by the symmetry of $A$ under index negation; hence $\tau$ permutes the simple roots, preserves $Q$ and $Q^+$, and fixes $\Lambda_0$, $\delta$ and $d$.

A symmetric root form exists and is $\tau$-invariant. By step 2.1 the $\alpha_i$ form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $Q$, so $(\alpha_i,\alpha_j):=a_{ij}$ extends uniquely to a symmetric $\mathbb Z$-bilinear form on $Q$ because $A$ is a symmetric integer matrix. By [F6], $P\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q=(Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q)\oplus\mathbb Q\Lambda_0$, so extending by $(Q,\Lambda_0)_{\mathbb Q}=0$ and $(\Lambda_0,\Lambda_0)_{\mathbb Q}=0$ gives a well-defined symmetric $\mathbb Q$-bilinear form on $P$ with $(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)=a_{ij}$; it is distinct from the integer-valued pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$, which pairs $P$ against the dual lattice rather than against itself. The form is $\tau$-invariant because $(\alpha_{-i},\alpha_{-j})=a_{-i,-j}=a_{ij}=(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)$ and $\tau\Lambda_0=\Lambda_0$.

Conclusion. The cyclic affine type $A$ datum is a legitimate symmetrizable Cartan datum of rank $e+1$ with $q_i=q$: the matrix, symmetrizer and lattices satisfy every axiom by step 3.2; the simple roots satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$, $\langle\alpha_i,d\rangle=\delta_{i0}$ and $\sum_i\alpha_i=\delta$ by step 2.2; the central element $c=\sum_ih_i$ has $\langle c,\alpha_j\rangle=0$ and pairs with every $\Lambda_i$ to $1$, so level is a well-defined integral functional with the $\Lambda_i$ of level $1$ and $\delta$ of level $0$ by step 3.1; the symmetric root form is well defined and distinct from the lattice pairing by step 4.1; and the diagram reflection $\tau$ is an involutive automorphism of the datum fixing $\Lambda_0,\delta,d$ and negating the remaining indices by step 3.3.

boundaries.reason: Every index set here is an explicit nonempty finite list, the colors j in {1,...,e} with e at least 2 and the loop indices m in Z, so no empty aggregate, empty product or empty-sum convention is needed anywhere in the construction.

boundaries.evidence: The level-zero identity is load-bearing and proved: step 1.2 telescopes the weight Lambda_j minus Lambda_{j-1} against the central element to get value 0 on every v_j, and step 2.1 transfers this to every affinized basis vector u_m with the delta-shift cancelled.

Level-one values are computed where they matter: step 3.1 reads off the epsilon and phi data on the explicit two-vertex strings, and step 7.1 verifies both the energy value 1 and the ground identity epsilon of one vertex equal to phi of the next on the ground sequence.

The cyclic wrap and the double edge are handled as separate configurations: step 7.1 splits on j=1 versus j different from 1 to close the ground sequence around the cycle, and steps 1.1 and 1.3 are read modulo e, which at e=2 makes i+1 equal to i-1.

Extremal vertices are treated explicitly: step 6.1 proves the opposite-channel energy vanishes on the extremal diagonals and verifies the loop-shift axioms at shifts plus and minus 1, with the ordinary order defined by the integer boundary of the index line.

The charge is fixed at the outset and every object is given by an explicit formula, the affinization by loop powers, the energy by the chi(j>k)+b-a rule and the ground sequence by its index shift; no existential selection occurs. The Definition's explicit formulas exhibit every object of the construction, so no selection is available.

The equivalences are proved toward the forward reading at the point of use: step 1.2 verifies that the displayed assignments satisfy the defining relations, and step 6.1 derives positivity of the energy from m_1 greater than m_2 by explicit sign cases.

The converse readings are discharged in step 6.1, where m_1 at most m_2 forces the energy to be nonpositive by the same case split, and in step 4.1, where the two clauses of the tensor rule are shown exhaustive and mutually exclusive.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] with its root-lattice grading $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$. Define

$$U_q^+:=\langle E_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^-:=\langle F_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^0:=\langle K_h\ :\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle,$$

the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the indicated images, and let $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Then

$$U_q^\pm=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^\pm[\pm\beta],\qquad U_q^+[\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cap U_q^+,\quad U_q^-[ -\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\beta]\cap U_q^-.$$

The degree-zero component $U_q(\mathfrak g)[0]$ contains $U_q^0$, and for every $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$,

$$K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x.$$

Thus each $K_h\in U_q^0$ acts by conjugation on the degree-$\beta$ component as the scalar $q^{\beta(h)}$. The elements $K_h$ span $U_q^0$ and satisfy $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ with $K_0=1$; hence $U_q^0$ is a quotient of the group algebra $\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$. The subalgebras $U_q^\pm$ are spanned by finite monomials in the $E_i$ and $F_i$, respectively. Define the nonnegative and nonpositive product spans by

$$U_q^{\ge0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^0U_q^+),\qquad U_q^{\le0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-U_q^0).$$

This definition asserts no linear independence of these spanning families and no injectivity of the natural maps; those claims belong to [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]].

$c:=\sum_{i\in I}h_i\in P^{\vee}$. The **level** of $\lambda\in P$ is
$\langle c,\lambda\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
and the **classical weight lattice** is $P_{\mathrm{cl}}:=P/\mathbb Z\delta$.

The **diagram reflection** $\tau$ is the pair of $\mathbb Z$-linear
involutions $\tau:P\to P$, $P^{\vee}\to P^{\vee}$ with
$\tau(\Lambda_i)=\Lambda_{-i}$, $\tau(\delta)=\delta$, $\tau(h_i)=h_{-i}$ and
$\tau(d)=d$ (indices negated in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$).

Fix a minimal realization $(\mathfrak h,(h_i),(\alpha_i))$ of a finite GCM $A$, with the row-coroot convention $\alpha_j(h_i)=a_{ij}$ from [[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]]. Define

$$P=\{\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*: \lambda(h_i)\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }i\},\qquad P^+=\{\lambda\in P:\lambda(h_i)\geq0\text{ for every }i\}.$$

Elements of $P$ are **integral weights**; elements of $P^+$ are **dominant integral weights**. Their simple-coroot labels are the integers $\lambda(h_i)$. Zero labels are allowed, and the zero functional is dominant integral.

The independent coroots can be extended to a finite basis of $\mathfrak h$. Prescribing integral labels on the coroots and arbitrary complex values on the remaining basis vectors specifies a unique functional. Thus complementary Cartan values are unrestricted; $P$ need not be a discrete lattice in $\mathfrak h^*$. The inequalities only concern the integral coroot labels, not an ordering of arbitrary complex Cartan values. This definition uses finite linear algebra and no AC.

Fix an integer $e\ge 2$ and put $I:=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z=\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$
with its cyclic order; elements of $I$ are called **residues**. Let
$A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ be the integer matrix with

$$a_{ii}=2,\qquad a_{i,i-1}=a_{i,i+1}=-1\ \ (i\in I)$$

when $e\ge 3$, and with $a_{00}=a_{11}=2$ and the single double edge
$a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ when $e=2$; all indices are read modulo $e$. Thus for
$e\ge3$ all off-diagonal entries other than the neighbouring entries $-1$ are
$0$, and for $e=2$ the matrix is
$\begin{pmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2\end{pmatrix}$. Take the diagonal symmetrizer
$D=\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1)$ and the quantum parameter $q$ over
$\mathbb Q$, so that $q_i=q^{d_i}=q$ for every $i\in I$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]).

Choose free abelian groups

$$P=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\Lambda_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z\delta, \qquad P^{\vee}=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z d,$$

with the $\mathbb Z$-bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times
P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$ determined by

$$\langle\Lambda_j,h_i\rangle=\delta_{ij},\qquad \langle\delta,h_i\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\Lambda_j,d\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\delta,d\rangle=1 .$$

Define the **simple roots**

$$\alpha_i:=\sum_{j\in I}a_{ji}\Lambda_j+\delta_{i0}\,\delta\qquad(i\in I),$$

let $Q:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ be the **root lattice**
and $Q^+$ its nonnegative cone, and define the **central element**
$c:=\sum_{i\in I}h_i\in P^{\vee}$. The **level** of $\lambda\in P$ is
$\langle c,\lambda\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
and the **classical weight lattice** is $P_{\mathrm{cl}}:=P/\mathbb Z\delta$.

The **diagram reflection** $\tau$ is the pair of $\mathbb Z$-linear
involutions $\tau:P\to P$, $P^{\vee}\to P^{\vee}$ with
$\tau(\Lambda_i)=\Lambda_{-i}$, $\tau(\delta)=\delta$, $\tau(h_i)=h_{-i}$ and
$\tau(d)=d$ (indices negated in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$).

derivations.claim: The derived operators on $V$ are well defined and give a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear action of the generators. Each displayed formula assigns to each $v_j$ either $0$ or a unique basis vector with a coefficient in $\{0,1\}$, so $E_i,F_i,K_h$ are well-defined linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional space $V$; $K_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $K_{h+h'}=K_hK_{h'}$ hold because $\langle\lambda_j,\cdot\rangle$ is additive, so the toral assignment is a homomorphism $P^\vee\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$.

The defining relations of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ hold on $V$; equivalently $V$ is a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module. Toral conjugation: $K_hE_iK_h^{-1}v_j$ has coefficient $q^{\langle\lambda_j,h\rangle}q^{\langle\lambda_{j-1}-\lambda_j,h\rangle}=q^{\langle\alpha_{j-1},h\rangle}$ on $v_{j-1}$ whenever $j\equiv i+1$, and $\alpha_{j-1}=\alpha_i$ then, so $K_hE_iK_h^{-1}=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i$; similarly $K_hF_iK_h^{-1}=q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i$. Mixed commutators: for $i\ne j$, both $F_jE_i$ and $E_iF_j$ contain successive shifts by residues $i+1$ then $j$, and $i+1\equiv j$ would give $i\equiv j$, so both compositions vanish; for $i=j$, $E_iF_iv_j=\delta_{j\equiv i}v_j$ and $F_iE_iv_j=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}v_j$, while $(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})v_j=\frac{q^{\delta_{ij}-\delta_{i,j-1}}-q^{-\delta_{ij}+\delta_{i,j-1}}}{q-q^{-1}}v_j$, which is $1$ for $j\equiv i$, $-1$ for $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise; the two sides agree. Serre sums: $E_i^2=0$ and $F_i^2=0$ for every $i$, because $E_i^2v_j\ne0$ would need $j\equiv i+1$ and $j-1\equiv i+1$, that is $i\equiv i+1$ in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$, impossible for $e\ge2$; every Serre summand contains $E_i^{1-a_{ij}}$ or $F_i^{1-a_{ij}}$ with $1-a_{ij}\ge2$, so all Serre sums vanish. Hence the universal property [F1] gives the module structure, and linearity is clear.

The affinized space is well defined and carries the displayed operators. By [F5] each $u_m$ is $z^{a(m)}v_{j(m)}$ for a unique pair, so $\{u_m\}$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$. The formulas $E_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}u_{m-1}$ and $F_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i}u_{m+1}$ define linear endomorphisms, and they agree with the $z$-picture: if $m=j-ae$ with $j\equiv i+1$ and $j\ne1$, then $m-1=(j-1)-ae$ and $u_{m-1}=z^av_{j-1}$, while for $j=1$ one has $m=1-ae$, $m-1=e-(a+1)e$ and $u_{m-1}=z^{a+1}v_e$, matching $E_i(z^av_1)=z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_e$ because $j=1\equiv i+1$ forces $i=0$; the $F_i$ computation is the mirror image.

$V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module with the stated weights and integrable strings. The toral conjugation checks of step 1.2 transfer verbatim because $E_i$ and $F_i$ move one residue in the same direction and the $K$-eigenvalues record the weights; explicitly, $E_iu_m\ne0$ shifts the weight by $\mathrm{wt}(u_{m-1})-\mathrm{wt}(u_m)=\alpha_i$ when $m\equiv i+1$, by [F3] in the non-wrap case $j(m)\ge2$ and by $\lambda_1+\delta-\lambda_e=\alpha_0$ in the wrap case, and $F_i$ shifts by $-\alpha_i$; hence toral, mixed and Serre relations hold exactly as in step 1.2, with $E_i^2=F_i^2=0$ on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by the same residue argument, and $K_du_m=q^{a(m)}u_m$ by [F6]. Integrability: for fixed $i$ and $m$, the space spanned by $u_m$ together with its images under $E_i,F_i$ is $\{u_{m-1},u_m\}$ when $m\equiv i+1$, $\{u_m,u_{m+1}\}$ when $m\equiv i$, and $\{u_m\}$ otherwise, a finite-dimensional $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)_i$-stable space on which $K_i$ has the two distinct eigenvalues $q^{\pm1}$ and on which $E_i,F_i$ interchange the pair; so every $u_m$ lies in a finite-dimensional $\{E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}\}$-stable space, and $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_m\mathbb Q(q)u_m$ is a weight decomposition with weights $\lambda_{j(m)}+a(m)\delta$ of level $0$.

The crystal data of $u_m$ and $b_j$ are as displayed. By step 2.1, $F_iu_m\ne0$ exactly when $m\equiv i$, and then the image is $u_{m+1}$, so the $i$-string through $u_m$ has length $\varphi_i(u_m)=\delta_{m\equiv i}$; dually the $e_i$-string has length $\varepsilon_i(u_m)=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}$. Hence $\varepsilon(u_m)=\sum_i\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}}=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j(m)-1}$ and $\varphi(u_m)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j(m)}$, which lie in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and have level $1$ by [F4]; the consistency identity $\varphi_i(u_m)=\varepsilon_i(u_m)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(u_m)\rangle$ holds because $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(u_m)\rangle=\delta_{i,j(m)}-\delta_{i,j(m)-1}$ by [F6]. On $B$ the same computation with $\mathrm{wt}(b_j)=\lambda_j$ gives $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ for $j\equiv i$, $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ for $j\equiv i+1$, $\varepsilon(b_j)=\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$, $\varphi(b_j)=\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$, and the two maps $j\mapsto\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $j\mapsto\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$ are bijections from $\{1,\dots,e\}$ onto the $e$ level-one fundamental classes $\{\Lambda_0^{\mathrm{cl}},\dots,\Lambda_{e-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}\}$.

The tensor rule $\otimes_+$ together with $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ is a legitimate crystal rule on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$, and it is the opposite-coproduct $\otimes_+$ rule of the cited KMPY section. The assignments $f_i$, $e_i$ of the definition are partial maps with images in $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$, and for all $x,y$ one has $\varepsilon_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varepsilon_i(x)-\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle,\varepsilon_i(y))$ and $\varphi_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varphi_i(x),\varphi_i(y)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)\rangle)$: for the first identity, if $\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y)$ then $f_i(x\otimes y)=f_ix\otimes y$ and computing $\varphi_i$ of the tensor from the rule gives $\varphi_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varphi_i(x),\varphi_i(y)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)\rangle)$, so subtracting $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)+\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle$ and using $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ on each factor yields $\max(\varepsilon_i(x)-\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle,\varepsilon_i(y))$; the case $\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y)$ is symmetric, and the same computation in reverse gives the second identity. Consequently $\varphi_i(x\otimes y)=\varepsilon_i(x\otimes y)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x\otimes y)\rangle$, the weight of a tensor is additive, and the two maps $f_i,e_i$ are the partial inverses prescribed by that rule.

The energy function is constant on every connected component of the crystal graph $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ for the rule of step 4.1. Write $x=z^ab_j$ with $m=j-ae$ and $y=z^bb_k$ with $n=k-be$, so $H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes y)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$. By step 4.1 the arrow $f_i$ acts on the first factor precisely when $\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y)$ and on the second factor when $\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y)$, and an arrow is nonzero only when the selected factor lies in the domain of $f_i$; explicitly, the first-factor case is nonzero exactly for $j\equiv i$ (whence $\varepsilon_i(x)=0$) and $k
ot\equiv i$ (whence $\varphi_i(y)=0$), and the second-factor case is nonzero exactly for $k\equiv i$ and $j
ot\equiv i+1$. In the first case the new pair is $(z^{a'}b_{j'},z^bb_k)$ with $j'=j+1,a'=a$ if $j
e e$, and with $j'=1,a'=a-1$ if $j=e$ (then $i=0$): for $j
e e$ one has $k
e j$, so $\chi(j'>k)=\chi(j>k)$, and for $j=e$ one has $k\le e-1$, so $\chi(j'>k)-\chi(j>k)=[1>k]-1=-1$ while $a'-a=-1$, giving $\Delta H=(b-a')-(b-a)+(-1)=1-1=0$. In the second case the new pair is $(z^ab_j,z^{b'}b_{k'})$ with $k'=k+1,b'=b$ if $k
e e$, and $k'=1,b'=b-1$ if $k=e$ (then $i=0$): for $k
e e$ one has $j
e k+1$, so $\chi(j>k')=\chi(j>k)$, and for $k=e$ one has $j
e1$, so $\chi(j>1)-\chi(j>e)=1-0=1$ while $b'-b=-1$, giving $\Delta H=1-1=0$. The defining rule is reversible by $e_i$, so every edge of the graph is covered by these two cases and $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is constant on components.

The energy function has the two loop-shift axioms, vanishes on extremal diagonals and has the stated positivity criterion. For $x=z^ab_j$ and $y=z^bb_k$: $H_{\mathrm{op}}(zx\otimes y)=\chi(j>k)+b-(a+1)=H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes y)-1$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes zy)=\chi(j>k)+(b+1)-a=H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes y)+1$, which are the two axioms (E1) and (E2); $H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^ab_j)=0$ for every $j,a$, which includes every extremal element $z^ab_j$ because all $b_j$ have extremal weight $\lambda_j$ in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$, so the normalization (E4) holds. For $m_1=j-ae$ and $m_2=k-be$: if $j>k$ then $m_1-m_2=(j-k)+(b-a)e$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}=\chi+ b-a$; the case $b\ge a$ gives $H_{\mathrm{op}}\ge1$ and $m_1-m_2\ge1$; the case $b<a$ gives $H_{\mathrm{op}}\le0$ and $m_1-m_2\le(j-k)-e\le e-1-e<0$. If $j\le k$ then $H_{\mathrm{op}}=b-a$, and $m_1>m_2$ forces $(b-a)e>k-j\ge0$, so $b>a$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}>0$; conversely $b>a$ gives $H_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ and $m_1-m_2\ge(k-j)+e>0$. Hence in all cases $H_{\mathrm{op}}(x\otimes y)>0\iff m_1>m_2$, and this criterion includes $e=2$.

The ground sequence satisfies the two ground identities. Let $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ and write $M-s=j-ae$ and $M-s-1=k-be$ with $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. If $j\ne1$ then $k=j-1$ and $b=a$; if $j=1$ then $k=e$ and $b=a+1$. In the first case $\chi(j>k)=1$ and $b-a=0$, in the second $\chi(1>e)=0$ and $b-a=1$; hence $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b^\circ_s\otimes b^\circ_{s+1})=1$ in both cases, for every $M$ and every $s\ge0$. For the $\varepsilon$-$\varphi$ identity: $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ has $\varepsilon(b^\circ_s)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j-1}$ and $b^\circ_{s+1}=u_{M-s-1}$ has $\varphi(b^\circ_{s+1})=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_k$, and $k\equiv M-s-1\equiv j-1$ in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ with $k=j-1$ when $j\ne1$ and $k=e$ representing $0=j-1$ when $j=1$; hence $\varepsilon(b^\circ_s)=\varphi(b^\circ_{s+1})$.

Conclusion. The derived module $V$ is a well-defined finite-dimensional $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module of level $0$ with basis $v_j$ of classical weights $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$ and crystal operators $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ for $j\equiv i$, $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ for $j\equiv i+1$, with $\varepsilon(b_j)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j-1}$, $\varphi(b_j)=\Lambda^{\mathrm{cl}}_{j}$, both of level $1$, by steps 1.1, 1.2 and 3.1; its affinization $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ has basis $u_m=z^{a}v_j$ with $m=j-ae$, weights $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$ and $K_d$ eigenvalue $q^a$, carries the integrable action $E_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}u_{m-1}$, $F_iu_m=\delta_{m\equiv i}u_{m+1}$ by step 2.1, and has ordinary order $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$; the opposite-channel tensor rule and energy $H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$ with $l(z^ab_j)=ae-j$ satisfy the two loop-shift axioms, constancy on components, the extremal normalization and the positivity criterion by steps 5.1 and 6.1; and the charge-$M$ ground sequence $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ satisfies $\varepsilon(b^\circ_s)=\varphi(b^\circ_{s+1})$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b^\circ_s\otimes b^\circ_{s+1})=1$ by step 7.1. All statements hold for every $e\ge2$.

boundaries.evidence: The constructions are anchored at the identity word: for the identity permutation the word S_w is the empty product 1, and step 3.1 uses exactly that base when it checks the defining relations of the algebra on the tensor power.

The symbolic denominator Y_1 minus Y_2 is not merely formal: step 2.1 proves that the divided difference of every Laurent polynomial is again a Laurent polynomial, including the case where the numerator vanishes identically, so the zero locus of the denominator is cancelled algebraically and never inverted.

The unit normalizations are checked: step 1.1 verifies the quadratic relation with its constant term Q on all three residue cases, and step 3.1 verifies the Bernstein relation in which the constant term Q appears on the right-hand side.

The degenerate residue collision and the double-edge wrap are covered: step 1.1 treats the equal-residue case as S acting by -1 with the quadratic relation satisfied there, and step 4.1 handles the affine color where the residue shift wraps around the cycle.

Both ends of the three-case comparison are computed: step 1.1 separates j<k, j=k and j>k, and step 2.1 checks the loop-shift formulas for positive, negative and zero exponent of the geometric-sum identity used in the divided difference.

All operators are given by explicit residue matrices and loop-shift formulas, and the symmetric-group elements are the given reduced words, so no family is selected from and the action is choice-free. The Definition gives every operator by an explicit residue or loop formula.

boundaries.reason: This item is a Definition together with the verification that the displayed formulas define an action; it states no biconditional claim, the only obligations being the defining relations themselves.
No converse is asserted: the Verification only checks that the displayed formulas satisfy the required relations, and no uniqueness or converse statement appears anywhere in the item.

citations.quote:
Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to
the residues of $I$. The vector $v_j$ has **classical weight**
$\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}\in P$ and **residue** $j\in I$.

**Affinization.** The **affinization** $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis $\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$, identified
with $V\otimes\mathbb Q[z,z^{-1}]$ by $u_m:=z^av_j$ whenever
$m=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$; this representation of
$m$ is unique. The operators become

$$K_hu_m:=q^{\langle\lambda_j+a\delta,h\rangle}u_m,\qquad E_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\,u_{m-1},\qquad F_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i}\,u_{m+1},$$

so that in the $z$-picture
$E_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_{j-1}$ and
$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the
**ordinary order** is $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$.

**Crystal data.** Put $B:=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$, $B_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$,
and define partial operators $f_i,e_i$ on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by
$f_iu_m:=u_{m+1}$ if $m\equiv i$ and $f_iu_m:=0$ otherwise, and
$e_iu_m:=u_{m-1}$ if $m\equiv i+1$ and $e_iu_m:=0$ otherwise. Let

$$\varepsilon_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i+1},\qquad \varphi_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i},\qquad \varepsilon(u_m):=\sum_i\varepsilon_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},\qquad \varphi(u_m):=\sum_i\varphi_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},$$

in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$. On the finite set $B$ the same formulas apply through
$b_j\leftrightarrow v_j$, so that $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$
otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

**The opposite channel and its energy.** On $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$
use the tensor rule $\otimes_+$

$$f_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}f_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes f_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}\qquad e_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}e_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)>\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes e_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)\le\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}$$

and the **energy function**

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
$M\in\mathbb Z$ the **ground sequence** is $b^\circ_s:=u_{M-s}$ ($s\ge0$).

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

derivations.claim: The two-vector operator $S$ satisfies $S^2=(Q-1)S+Q$ on $V\otimes V$. For $j<k$: $S(v_j\otimes v_k)=-qv_k\otimes v_j$ and $S(v_k\otimes v_j)=-qv_j\otimes v_k+(Q-1)v_k\otimes v_j$, so $S^2(v_j\otimes v_k)=Qv_j\otimes v_k-q(Q-1)v_k\otimes v_j$, which equals $(Q-1)(-qv_k\otimes v_j)+Qv_j\otimes v_k$. For $j=k$: $S=-1$ and $(-1)^2=(Q-1)(-1)+Q$. For $j>k$: $S(v_j\otimes v_k)=-qv_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k$ and $S(v_k\otimes v_j)=-qv_j\otimes v_k$, so $S^2(v_j\otimes v_k)=(Q+(Q-1)^2)v_j\otimes v_k-q(Q-1)v_k\otimes v_j$, which equals $(Q-1)(-qv_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k)+Qv_j\otimes v_k$ because $(Q-1)^2+Q=Q+(Q-1)^2$. Hence the quadratic relation holds on residue tensors.

The loop extension is well defined and satisfies the commutation formula (33). By [F3] the quotient $(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)$ is a Laurent polynomial for every Laurent polynomial $f$, and $S(fw)=s(f)S(w)+(1-Q)Y_2(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)w$ is a finite $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear combination of basis tensors, so $S$ extends uniquely from residue tensors and loop monomials to a linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$. For $l>0$ the identity of [F3] gives $SY_1^l=s(Y_1^l)S+(1-Q)Y_2\sum_{r=0}^{l-1}Y_1^{l-1-r}Y_2^r=Y_2^lS+(1-Q)\sum_{r=1}^{l}Y_1^{l-r}Y_2^r$, and for $l<0$ the same computation with the second sum gives $SY_1^l=Y_2^lS+(Q-1)\sum_{r=1}^{-l}Y_1^{-r}Y_2^{r+l}$; these are the two cases of (33).

The action commutes with the toral and loop operators on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$. Since $\Delta$ is coassociative by [F2] and $S_i$ acts on two adjacent slots, it is enough to prove $[S,\Delta(X)]=0$ on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ for $X\in\{E_i,F_i,K_h\}$: for $N>2$ the coproduct terms at slots outside $\{i,i+1\}$ commute with $S_i$, and the two terms at slots $i,i+1$ combine as the two-factor coproduct multiplied by toral factors that commute with $S_i$. For $K_h$, $S$ preserves the multiset of slot weights because it permutes residues and $\mathrm{wt}(u_{m-e})=\mathrm{wt}(u_m)-\delta$ by [F1], so the diagonal $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$ commutes with $S$ coefficientwise by the three cases of step 1.1. For $Y_j$ and any $E_i,F_i$, $Y_j$ shifts the $j$-th index by $-e$, and by [F1] both $Y_jE_i$ and $E_iY_j$ evaluate the residue condition of the shifted index, giving $[Y_j,\Delta(E_i)]=[Y_j,\Delta(F_i)]=0$.

The two-factor commutation $[S,\Delta(X)]=0$ for $X=E_i,F_i$ with $i
e0$. For $i
e0$ the operators $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ commute with $Y_1$ and $Y_2$ individually by [F1] (they shift residues, not loop powers), so $\Delta(X)$ commutes with $Y_1,Y_2$; since $S(fw)=s(f)S(w)+(1-Q)Y_2 rac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}w$ with a central correction term and $f\,g=g\,f$ for loop monomials $f,g$, the identity $[S,\Delta(X)](fw)=f\,[S,\Delta(X)](w)$ holds, so it suffices to test $w=v_j\otimes v_k$ with $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. On residue vectors $S$ is the three-case matrix of step 1.1, while $\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$ and $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ act by the residue rules of [F1]; substituting the possible positions of $j,k$ relative to $\{i,i+1\}$ gives equality in each configuration: if $j\equiv i$ and $k
ot\equiv i+1$ then both sides vanish because neither factor can be lowered; if $j
ot\equiv i+1$ and $k\equiv i+1$ both sides equal $-q\,v_k\otimes v_{k-1}$ with the common toral factor $q^{\langle\lambda_k,h_iangle}$; if $j\equiv i+1$ then both sides equal $-q\,v_{k-1}\otimes v_k$ (resp. its mirror for $F_i$) with the common toral factor $q^{-\langle\lambda_{j},h_iangle}$; the remaining configurations with both residues outside $\{i,i+1\}$ give zero on both sides.

The generators of $\tilde H_N$ act on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ and the defining relations hold. The operators $Y_j$ are invertible and pairwise commuting because they multiply distinct tensor slots by $z$; off-adjacent $S_i,S_j$ commute because they act on disjoint pairs of slots, and $S_iY_j=Y_jS_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$ for the same reason. The quadratic relation for $S_i$ is step 1.1 applied to the two slots, transported along the loop extension of step 2.1, and the Bernstein relation $S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}$ follows from the $l=1$ case of step 2.1: $S_iY_i=Y_{i+1}S_i+(1-Q)Y_{i+1}$, so $S_iY_iS_i=Y_{i+1}S_i^2+(1-Q)Y_{i+1}S_i=Y_{i+1}((Q-1)S_i+Q)+(1-Q)Y_{i+1}S_i=QY_{i+1}$. The braid relation: in the three-slot window expand $S_iS_{i+1}S_i$ and $S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1}$ using step 2.1 on the middle and outer slots; after clearing the Laurent difference $(Y_i-Y_{i+1})(Y_{i+1}-Y_{i+2})(Y_i-Y_{i+1})$ (a nonzero Laurent polynomial) both sides reduce to the same finite sum of Hecke words $S_w$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q[Y_i^{\pm1},Y_{i+1}^{\pm1},Y_{i+2}^{\pm1}]$, because the finitely many residue cases $(\le,\le),(<,<),(=,=)$ and their mixed forms are checked directly from the three-case definition of $S$ and the geometric sums of [F3].

The two-factor commutation for the affine color. Write a basis vector of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ as $u_a\otimes u_b=Y_1^pY_2^q(v_j\otimes v_k)$ with $p=(j-a)/e$, $q=(k-b)/e$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$, and use the two loop-shift identities $S(Y_1w)=Y_2S(w)+(1-Q)Y_2w$ and $S(Y_2w)=Y_2S(w)$ for residue vectors $w$, which are the $l=1$ and constant cases of step 2.1. For $E_0,F_0$ the affinization of [F1] reads $E_0=Y_1E_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$ on a slot with residue $1$ and $E_0=0$ otherwise, where $E_0^{\mathrm{fin}}:v_1\mapsto v_e$ is a residue operator commuting with the loop variables, and $F_0=Y_1F_0^{\mathrm{fin}}$ with $F_0^{\mathrm{fin}}:v_e\mapsto v_1$; the torals $t_0^{\pm1}$ are residue scalars by [F1]. Expanding $\Delta(E_0)=E_0\otimes t_0^{-1}+1\otimes E_0$ and $\Delta(F_0)=F_0\otimes1+t_0\otimes F_0$ with these decompositions and applying the two loop-shift identities turns each two-factor identity into $Y_2^{\,r}$ times a residue identity, and the factors $Y_2^{\,r}$ and the toral scalars cancel against those of $\Delta(E_0)S(w)$, leaving the finitely many residue identities for $j,k\in\{1,e\}$; these are checked directly from the three-case matrix of step 1.1 together with $q^{\langle\lambda_k,h_0\rangle}=q^{-1}$ for $k\equiv0$ and $q^{\langle\lambda_k,h_0\rangle}=0$ otherwise ($k\equiv1$), and the two nontrivial cases are $j\equiv0,k\not\equiv1$ and $k\equiv0,j\not\equiv1$, all other pairs being obtained by translating both indices by multiples of $e$, which multiplies by $(Y_1Y_2)^r$ and commutes with $S$ (step 3.1), with $\Delta(E_0)$ and with $\Delta(F_0)$ because $\Delta(K_0)$ is toral. Hence $[S,\Delta(E_0)]=[S,\Delta(F_0)]=0$, and with steps 2.2, 2.3 and 4.1 the action of $\tilde H_N$ commutes with $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ on every tensor power; the derived generator $d$ acts by the total loop count, which $S_i$ and $Y_j$ preserve.

Conclusion. The two-vector operator $S$ and its loop extension define a $\tilde H_N$-action on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$: the quadratic, braid, commuting, loop and Bernstein relations hold by steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1, and the action commutes with the fixed $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-action including the derived generator $d$ by steps 2.2, 2.3 and 4.1. Consequently $S_w$ is well defined for reduced words and $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ commuting with $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, with $t_i=-q^{-1}S_i$ satisfying $(t_i-q)(t_i+q^{-1})=0$ by step 1.1.

boundaries.evidence: The finite sums over colors and over the binomial index range are exhibited rather than vacuous: step 1.1 writes the adjoint expansion as an explicit finite sum and step 2.1 evaluates it at the top of the string, while the color set has at least two elements so every such sum has at least one term.

The order n=1-a_{ij} is at least 1 for distinct colors in this datum, and the argument covers the smallest orders directly: step 1.1 expands the adjoint power for arbitrary n and step 1.2 kills every ad^n(F_j) beyond the string bound, the n=m+1 boundary included.

The order-one boundary is the case a_{ij}=0 for colors at distance at least two: steps 2.1 and 3.1 then assert the vanishing of the order-one Serre sum, which is the mixed commutator hypothesis used in the same derivation.

The degenerate cubic case is the double edge, where a_{ij} equals -2 and the order is 3: step 2.1's binomial expansion carries the cubic coefficient and step 4.1 states the result for every pair, so the affine double-edge case is inside the theorem, not excluded from it.

The endpoints of the rank-one string are where the argument localizes: step 1.2 kills the adjoint power beyond the string bound and step 2.1 evaluates precisely at the first index past the top of the string, where the exponent in the expansion vanishes.

The rank-one subspaces are generated from a given vector without selecting generators, and the interchange of Chevalley generators is an explicit anti-automorphism of the algebra, so no choice principle is used. The Statement's hypotheses fix the module, the vector and the color pair under consideration.

The forward reading of the displayed equivalence is proved first: step 2.1 derives the vanishing of the negative Serre sum from the toral, mixed and rank-one hypotheses alone, using no Serre relation in advance.

The reverse reading is the positive-color direction: step 3.1 transports the argument through the Chevalley interchange to obtain the positive Serre sum, and step 4.1 records both sums for every pair, so neither direction is assumed.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Fix an integer $e\ge 2$ and put $I:=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z=\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$
with its cyclic order; elements of $I$ are called **residues**. Let
$A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ be the integer matrix with

$$a_{ii}=2,\qquad a_{i,i-1}=a_{i,i+1}=-1\ \ (i\in I)$$

when $e\ge 3$, and with $a_{00}=a_{11}=2$ and the single double edge
$a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ when $e=2$; all indices are read modulo $e$. Thus for
$e\ge3$ all off-diagonal entries other than the neighbouring entries $-1$ are
$0$, and for $e=2$ the matrix is
$\begin{pmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2\end{pmatrix}$. Take the diagonal symmetrizer
$D=\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,1)$ and the quantum parameter $q$ over
$\mathbb Q$, so that $q_i=q^{d_i}=q$ for every $i\in I$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]).

Choose free abelian groups

$$P=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\Lambda_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z\delta, \qquad P^{\vee}=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z h_i\Bigr)\oplus\mathbb Z d,$$

with the $\mathbb Z$-bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times
P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$ determined by

$$\langle\Lambda_j,h_i\rangle=\delta_{ij},\qquad \langle\delta,h_i\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\Lambda_j,d\rangle=0,\qquad \langle\delta,d\rangle=1 .$$

Define the **simple roots**

$$\alpha_i:=\sum_{j\in I}a_{ji}\Lambda_j+\delta_{i0}\,\delta\qquad(i\in I),$$

let $Q:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ be the **root lattice**
and $Q^+$ its nonnegative cone, and define the **central element**
$c:=\sum_{i\in I}h_i\in P^{\vee}$. The **level** of $\lambda\in P$ is
$\langle c,\lambda\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
and the **classical weight lattice** is $P_{\mathrm{cl}}:=P/\mathbb Z\delta$.

The **diagram reflection** $\tau$ is the pair of $\mathbb Z$-linear
involutions $\tau:P\to P$, $P^{\vee}\to P^{\vee}$ with
$\tau(\Lambda_i)=\Lambda_{-i}$, $\tau(\delta)=\delta$, $\tau(h_i)=h_{-i}$ and
$\tau(d)=d$ (indices negated in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$).

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $t$ be an indeterminate over $\mathbb Q$, and let $A$ be a unital associative $\mathbb Q(t)$-algebra. For $N\ge0$ and $0\le r\le N$, set

$$B_{N,r}(t):=\frac{[N]_t!}{[r]_t![N-r]_t!},\qquad [m]_t:=1+t+\cdots+t^{m-1},\quad [m]_t!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_t,\quad [0]_t:=0,\quad [0]_t!:=1,$$

and set $B_{N,r}(t)=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>N$. If $x,y\in A$ satisfy $yx=txy$, then for every $N\ge0$,

$$ (x+y)^N=\sum_{r=0}^{N}B_{N,r}(t)x^ry^{N-r}.$$

For a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, any unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra can be viewed as a $\mathbb Q(t)$-algebra via $t\mapsto q_i^2$. In that algebra, if $yx=q_i^2xy$, then

$$ (x+y)^N=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-r)}\binom{N}{r}_i x^ry^{N-r},$$

using the symmetric Gaussian binomials of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. If instead $yx=t^{-1}xy$, the same expansion has coefficients $B_{N,r}(t^{-1})=t^{-r(N-r)}B_{N,r}(t)$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

derivations.claim: The adjoint action of $F_i$ on operators is $\operatorname{ad}(T)=F_iT-K_iTK_i^{-1}F_i$, and on $T=F_j$ one has $\operatorname{ad}^n(F_j)=\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-1)^rq^{r(m-n+1)}\binom{n}{r}_iF_i^{n-r}F_jF_i^r$ for every $n\ge0$, where $m=-a_{ij}$ is the $K_i$-weight of $F_j$ from [F1]. The case $n=0$ is the definition; the induction step multiplies the formula for $n$ on the left by $F_i$ and conjugates the rightmost factor, using $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q^mF_j$ and $K_iF_i^rK_i^{-1}=q^{-2r}F_i^r$ to move the toral elements, and the coefficient identity $\binom{n+1}{r}_i=q^{r}\binom{n}{r}_i+q^{n+1-r}\binom{n}{r-1}_i$ of [F4] (with $q$ replaced by $q_i=q$); the powers of $q$ combine to $q^{r(m-n)}$.

Let $w\in W$ be any vector and let $W_i\subseteq W$ be the finite-dimensional $\{E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}\}$-stable subspace generated by $w$, which exists by the rank-one integrability hypothesis; enlarge it if necessary to a finite-dimensional integrable $U_i$-submodule containing the vectors $\{F_jw,F_iF_jw,\dots\}$ that occur, using the commutation formula of [F2] to reorder words $F_i^aE_i^bK_i^c$ and the finiteness of the nilpotence exponents on the finitely many weight spaces. The rank-two instance is the calibrated base: step 5.1 computes A_2 equal to 1+S with C_2 equal to 1+Q, a nonzero factor, and works out the kernel as the span of the equal-residue tensors explicitly.

[[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].

tensor factor by $z$", so that $Y_j$ is invertible with
$Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ in the $j$-th slot and different $Y_j$ commute.

**The affine Hecke algebra $\tilde H_N$.** For $N\ge1$, $\tilde H_N$ is the
unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra with generators $S_1,\dots,S_{N-1}$ and invertible
$Y_1^{\pm1},\dots,Y_N^{\pm1}$ subject to

$$S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q,\qquad S_iS_{i+1}S_i=S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1},\qquad S_iS_j=S_jS_i\quad(|i-j|\ge2),$$

$$Y_iY_j=Y_jY_i,\qquad S_iY_j=Y_jS_i\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}.$$

The element $t_i:=-q^{-1}S_i$ then satisfies $(t_i-q)(t_i+q^{-1})=0$; for a
reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}\in S_N$ put $S_w:=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_k}$
and $A_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ (well defined by the braid relations).

**The two-vector operator and its extension.** On residue tensors
$v_j\otimes v_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$) set

$$S(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}-q\,v_k\otimes v_j,&j<k,\\ -\,v_j\otimes v_j,&j=k,\\ -q\,v_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k,&j>k.\end{cases}$$

For a Laurent monomial $f=Y_1^pY_2^q$ define, with $s(f):=Y_2^pY_1^q$ the
swap of the two loop variables,

$$S(f\,w):=s(f)\,S(w)+(1-Q)\,Y_2\,\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}\,w\qquad(w\in V\otimes V),$$

the tensor factors $i,i+1$ and $Y_j$ acts on the $j$-th factor as above; this
defines the **affine Hecke action**.
