derivations.claim: $A_NS_i=S_iA_N=QA_N$. Since left and right multiplication by $S_i$ permute the set $\{S_w\}$ and the length pairing is symmetric, it suffices to prove the right version. Split $S_N$ into $\{w:l(ws_i)>l(w)\}$ and $\{w:l(ws_i)<l(w)\}$; these sets are exchanged by $w\mapsto ws_i$, and [F2] gives $A_NS_i=\sum_{l(ws_i)>l(w)}S_{ws_i}+\sum_{l(ws_i)<l(w)}(S_{ws_i}+(Q-1)S_w)$; the first sum is $\sum_{l(us_i)<l(u)}S_u$, so it combines with the leading term of the second sum to give $A_N$, and the remaining term is $(Q-1)A_N$; hence $A_NS_i=A_N+(Q-1)A_N=QA_N$. Multiplying $A_N=\sum_wS_w$ on the right by $A_N$ and using $\sum_i$ over reduced words gives $A_N^2=C_NA_N$ with $C_N=\sum_wQ^{l(w)}=\prod_{r=1}^N(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})$, the standard product formula for the Poincare polynomial of $S_N$.

$\sum_i\ker(S_i+1)\subseteq\ker A_N$. By step 1.1, $A_NS_i=QA_N$, so $A_N(S_i+1)=(Q+1)A_N$ and also $(S_i+1)A_N=(1+Q)A_N$; hence if $(S_i+1)x=0$ then $A_Nx=A_N(S_i+1)x/(Q+1)=0$. Since the sum of subspaces of the kernel lies in the kernel, the inclusion follows.

For every $x$ and $i$, $(S_i-Q)x\in\ker(S_i+1)$; modulo $J:=\sum_i\ker(S_i+1)$ one has $xS_w\equiv Q^{l(w)}x$ and $xA_N\equiv C_Nx$ for all $w\in S_N$. The first claim is $(S_i+1)(S_i-Q)=S_i^2+(1-Q)S_i-Q=0$ by [F1]. For the second, use induction on $l(w)$ with [F2]: if $w=us_i$ with $l(w)=l(u)+1$ then modulo $J$, $uS_i\equiv uQ$ because $(S_i-Q)u\in\ker(S_i+1)$ and $u$ commutes with $S_i-Q$; hence $xS_w=xuS_i\equiv Q\,xu$. Summing over $w$ with weights $Q^{l(w)}$ gives the displayed congruences.

$\ker A_N=J$. The inclusion $J\subseteq\ker A_N$ is step 2.1. Conversely let $A_Nx=0$; by step 2.2, $xA_N\equiv C_Nx\pmod J$, so $C_Nx\in J$; since $C_N\ne0$ by [F3] and $J$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspace, $x\in J$. Hence the kernel is exactly the sum of the two-eigen kernels of the $S_i$.

The splitting. By step 3.1 and step 2.2, $A_N$ kills $J=\ker A_N$; by step 1.1, $A_N^2=C_NA_N$ with $C_N\ne0$, so $P_N=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is idempotent. An idempotent on a vector space over a field gives $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}=\ker P_N\oplus\operatorname{im}P_N$, and $\ker P_N=\ker A_N$, $\operatorname{im}P_N=\operatorname{im}A_N$ because $C_N$ is a nonzero scalar; on $\operatorname{im}A_N$ the operator $A_N$ acts by $C_N$, since $A_N(A_Ny)=C_NA_Ny$. Since $A_N$ commutes with $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ by [F3], both summands are $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-submodules, and the canonical map $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}/\ker A_N\to\operatorname{im}A_N$ is a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-linear isomorphism.

The two-factor picture. Take $N=2$, so $S=S_1$, $A_2=1+S$ and $C_2=1+Q$. In the quotient by $\ker(S+1)$ the relation $S=-1$ holds, and [F4] gives $v_j\otimes v_j\in\ker(S+1)$ for every $j$; for $j<k$ the vector $v_j\otimes v_k-qv_k\otimes v_j$ lies in $\ker(S+1)$ because $S(v_j\otimes v_k-qv_k\otimes v_j)=-qv_k\otimes v_j+q^2v_j\otimes v_k=-(v_j\otimes v_k-qv_k\otimes v_j)$; conversely any vector in $\ker(S+1)$ is a linear combination of these elements and their loop multiples: writing an element of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ as $\sum_{a,b}f_{ab}(Y)u_a\otimes u_b$, the operator $S+1$ preserves the filtration by the finite-dimensional subspaces spanned by $u_a\otimes u_b$ with $|a|,|b|\le M$ up to loop shifts, and on each finite piece [F5] gives $\ker(S+1)=\ker(S-Q)^\perp$ with both spaces spanned by the listed residue vectors and their $Y$-multiples; the three cases $j<k$, $j=k$, $j>k$ of [F4] then give, in the quotient, $u_m\wedge u_m=0$, $u_l\wedge u_m=-u_m\wedge u_l$ when $m-l$ is a multiple of $e$, $u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l$ when $l,m$ lie in distinct adjacent-residue classes with $m<l+e$, and the remaining case is the full three-term straightening recurrence stated in the finite q-wedge definition below, obtained from the Bernstein identity $S_iY_i^l=Y_{i+1}^lS_i+(1-Q)\sum_{r=1}^{l}Y_i^{l-r}Y_{i+1}^r$; at $q=1$ the operator $S$ becomes the transposition, $C_N=N!$ and the kernel is the ordinary symmetric subspace.

Conclusion. $A_N^2=C_NA_N$ with $C_N=\prod_r(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})\ne0$, $A_NS_i=S_iA_N=QA_N$, $\ker A_N=\sum_i\ker(S_i+1)$, and $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}=\ker A_N\oplus\operatorname{im}A_N$ with quotient identified with $\operatorname{im}A_N$ and $A_N$ acting there by $C_N$, all proved without any torsion-freeness over a Laurent ring and without passing to an $A_0$-quotient; the two-factor kernel is the partial q-symmetric subspace and its quotient carries the three straightening cases.

boundaries.reason: The crystal is the explicit list of e basis vectors with e at least two and the affinized index set is Z, so neither is empty, and the tensor square used for connectedness is nonempty; no empty-set or empty-product boundary enters.

boundaries.evidence: Vanishing is verified rather than assumed: step 1.3 checks that the generators send each v_j to zero or to one basis vector and that divided powers of order at least two vanish, and step 1.2 closes the tensor square using the cases where one side's arrow is zero.

Level one is the load-bearing hypothesis: step 1.1 computes that every epsilon and phi value is a level-one dominant weight and that the two maps are bijections onto the level-one dominant weights, with the minimum set equal to the whole crystal.

The degenerate a=0 boundary of the affinized chart is the base of the lattice: step 2.1 defines the bar involution on the span of all loop shifts and checks it on the unshifted basis vectors as well as on every shifted one, including the two-color swap at e=2.

The extremal weights of the finite Weyl orbit are included: step 1.1 checks the bijection onto the level-one dominant weights at both boundary classes of the orbit, and the parametrization by loop exponent is single-valued at exponent zero.

The basis is given by the explicit assignment G(b_j)=v_j and the lattice by its displayed span, while the bar involution is defined by inverting q and fixing the basis; no selection is made, so the lower-basis package is choice-free. The Definition's displayed basis and span carry the whole construction.

boundaries.reason: The item states structural properties of a fixed crystal and a fixed basis; it asserts no biconditional, so there is no forward branch of an equivalence to discharge.
No converse implication appears: perfectness, connectedness and the lower-basis axioms are each verified in the numbered steps, and no if-and-only-if is claimed between them.

citations.quote:
Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to
the residues of $I$. The vector $v_j$ has **classical weight**
$\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}\in P$ and **residue** $j\in I$.

**Affinization.** The **affinization** $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis $\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$, identified
with $V\otimes\mathbb Q[z,z^{-1}]$ by $u_m:=z^av_j$ whenever
$m=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$; this representation of
$m$ is unique. The operators become

$$K_hu_m:=q^{\langle\lambda_j+a\delta,h\rangle}u_m,\qquad E_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\,u_{m-1},\qquad F_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i}\,u_{m+1},$$

so that in the $z$-picture
$E_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_{j-1}$ and
$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the
**ordinary order** is $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$.

**Crystal data.** Put $B:=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$, $B_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$,
and define partial operators $f_i,e_i$ on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by
$f_iu_m:=u_{m+1}$ if $m\equiv i$ and $f_iu_m:=0$ otherwise, and
$e_iu_m:=u_{m-1}$ if $m\equiv i+1$ and $e_iu_m:=0$ otherwise. Let

$$\varepsilon_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i+1},\qquad \varphi_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i},\qquad \varepsilon(u_m):=\sum_i\varepsilon_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},\qquad \varphi(u_m):=\sum_i\varphi_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},$$

in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$. On the finite set $B$ the same formulas apply through
$b_j\leftrightarrow v_j$, so that $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$
otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

**The opposite channel and its energy.** On $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$
use the tensor rule $\otimes_+$

$$f_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}f_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes f_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}\qquad e_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}e_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)>\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes e_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)\le\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}$$

and the **energy function**

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
$M\in\mathbb Z$ the **ground sequence** is $b^\circ_s:=u_{M-s}$ ($s\ge0$).

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: Perfectness of $B$ except connectedness. By [F1] every $\varepsilon(b_j)=\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\varphi(b_j)=\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$ has level one, and the two maps are bijections $\{1,\dots,e\}\to\{\Lambda_0^{\mathrm{cl}},\dots,\Lambda_{e-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}\}=(P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+)_1$ because both $j\mapsto\Lambda_j^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $j\mapsto\Lambda_{j-1}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ run through the $e$ fundamental classes; hence $B_{\min}=\{b:\langle c,\varepsilon(b)\rangle=1\}=B$ and axiom (P3) holds. For (P1): the weights $\lambda_j$ of $V$ are pairwise distinct with multiplicity one by [F1], and the finite Weyl group of the finite subdiagram acts transitively on them (it permutes the indices $j$ of the fundamental classes and hence the differences $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$), so they form the finite Weyl orbit of $\lambda^\circ$ with one-dimensional weight spaces, contained in its convex hull.

Connectedness of $B\otimes B$ for the fixed coproduct. Use the tensor rule $f_i(x\otimes y)=f_ix\otimes y$ if $\varphi_i(x)>\varepsilon_i(y)$ and $x\otimes f_iy$ otherwise, and $e_i(x\otimes y)=e_ix\otimes y$ if $\varphi_i(x)\ge\varepsilon_i(y)$ and $x\otimes e_iy$ otherwise. For a pair $(b_a,b_b)$ with $a>b$ use $i=b$: $\varphi_b(b_a)=0\ge\varepsilon_b(b_b)=0$, so $e_b$ acts on the first factor and $(b_a,b_b)\mapsto(b_{a-1},b_b)$; iterating lowers the first index to $b$. For $a<b$ use $f_b$: $\varphi_b(b_a)=0\le\varepsilon_b(b_b)=0$, so the rule acts on the second factor, $(b_a,b_b)\mapsto(b_a,b_{b+1})$, and iterating raises the second index to $a$. Hence every pair reaches the diagonal $(b_a,b_a)$; from $(b_j,b_j)$ the two arrows $f_j$ (first factor, using $\varphi_j(b_j)=1>0=\varepsilon_j(b_j)$) and then $f_j$ (second factor, using $\varphi_j(b_{j+1})=0\le\varepsilon_j(b_j)=0$) reach $(b_{j+1},b_{j+1})$, so all diagonal pairs are connected to each other and $B\otimes B$ is connected.

Lower global basis of $V$. Define $\overline{\cdot}$ by $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $\overline{v_j}=v_j$. Since $E_iv_j,F_iv_j\in\{0\}\cup\{v_{j\pm1}\}$, one has $\overline{E_iv}=\overline{E_i}\overline{v}$ and $\overline{F_iv}=\overline{F_i}\overline{v}$ for all $v$ because the coefficients $1$ are bar-invariant; the $A_0$-lattice $V_0=\bigoplus\mathbb Z[q]v_j$ satisfies $L:=\sum_jA_0v_j=V_0$ and $B$ is recovered as $\{v_j\bmod qV_0\}$, so $(V_0,B)$ is a crystal lattice by [F3]. By [F2] the $i$-string through any $v_j$ is exactly two-dimensional with $E_i$ and $F_i$ coefficients $1$: $E_iv_{i+1}=v_i$, $F_iv_i=v_{i+1}$ (indices mod $e$), and $E_i^2=F_i^2=0$ because the residue condition of two consecutive applications fails; hence $E_i^{(m)}=F_i^{(m)}=0$ for $m\ge2$ and the divided operators have the integral coefficient matrices $e_i,f_i$ with entries in $\{0,1\}$. This is exactly the lower-basis condition of [F3] with $G(b_j)=v_j$.

The affinized chart. Put $L_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\bigoplus_m\mathbb Z[q]u_m$ and $G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j=u_{j-ae}$; extend the bar involution by $\overline z=z$. Then $\overline{\cdot}$ is semilinear with coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, fixes every $G(z^ab_j)$, and satisfies $\overline{E_iw}=E_i\overline w$, $\overline{F_iw}=F_i\overline w$ for $w\in V_{\mathrm{aff}}$: the only loop shift occurs for $i=0$, where $E_0(z^av_1)=z^{a+1}v_e$ and $\overline{z^{a+1}v_e}=z^{a+1}v_e=E_0\overline{z^av_1}$, and the remaining cases have coefficients in $\{0,1\}$. The weight of $G(z^ab_j)$ is $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$, and the string bound of step 1.3 is unchanged because the $i$-orbits are the same two-vertex sets shifted by loops. The finite module $V$ carries only the $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$-weights $\lambda_j$ and no dominant level-one highest weight vector, so it is a level-$0$ $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-module and not a level-one $P$-graded highest weight module; the $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and $A_0=\mathbb Z[q]$ charts are used separately and are not identified.

Conclusion. The level-$0$ vector module has the level-one perfect crystal $B=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$ with the explicit $\varepsilon,\varphi$, connected tensor square and $B_{\min}=B$; the basis $G(b_j)=v_j$ is a lower global basis of $V$ whose $i$-strings have two vertices with coefficients $1$ and whose divided operators of order $\ge2$ vanish; and the affinized chart $G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j$ has the same properties with the full $P$-weight.

boundaries.evidence: The one-term boundary of the recursion is handled: the pair profile acts on unordered pairs, so a tuple of length at most one is already normal and the recursion performs no rewrite, and the spanning statement is made for every N at least 1.

Zero coefficients and zero corrections are handled: step 1.1's equal-residue case carries no correction terms, and step 2.1's fourth relation is applied only when both the quotient and the residue difference are positive, with the interior pair strictly between the endpoints.

The two unit coefficients are the cases of the displayed relations: the equal-residue case has coefficient -1 and the unequal-residue case has coefficient -q^{-1}, both appearing in step 1.1's case list, so the boundary coefficients are exhibited rather than generic.

The degenerate e=2 read of the gap is included: for e=2 the residue difference is 0 or 1 only, so the fourth relation is vacuous exactly when the two indices share a residue, which step 1.1 handles by the equal-residue case.

The recursion keeps every index inside the original extremes: step 3.1 proves each rewriting step preserves the index interval and strictly decreases the gap, so the outer endpoints of the pair are never passed.
The quotient, the two lattice charts and the rewriting rules are all defined by explicit spans and formulas, so the normal-ordering definition selects nothing.

The item's displayed energy criterion is used in its forward direction inside the rewrite: step 2.1 applies the three-term relation precisely for pairs whose opposite-channel energy is positive, and step 4.1 records the equivalence of the two formulations on the quotient.

The converse direction is the termination statement: step 3.1's well-founded gap measure shows every unordered pair is rewritten toward decreasing indices using only the cases of nonpositive energy, so no pair with decreasing indices is left unattended.

citations.quote:
Let $\tilde H_N$ act on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ as in
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]],
put $Q=q^2$, let $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$, and let
$C_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}Q^{l(w)}=\prod_{r=1}^{N}(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})\ne0$.
Then:

(i) $A_N^2=C_NA_N$, and $A_NS_i=S_iA_N=QA_N$ for every $i$; the operator
$P_N:=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear idempotent commuting with
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

(ii) $\ker A_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\ker(S_i+1)$; equivalently, on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$
the kernel of the q-antisymmetrizer is exactly the sum of the two-eigen kernels.

(iii) $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}=\ker A_N\oplus\operatorname{im}A_N$, and the
quotient by $\ker A_N$ is naturally identified with $\operatorname{im}A_N$, on
which $A_N$ acts by the scalar $C_N$. For $N=2$ the kernel $\ker(S_1+1)$ is
spanned by the loop multiples of the partial q-symmetric vectors
$v_j\otimes v_j$ and $v_j\otimes v_k-q\,v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j<k)$, and in the
quotient the three straightening cases of the finite q-wedge definition below hold: the images
of $v_j\otimes v_j$ vanish, and a pair $l<m$ is rewritten as in the three cases
of that definition. At $q=1$ all of this is the ordinary antisymmetrization:
$C_N=N!$ and $\ker A_N$ is the span of the ordinary symmetric tensors.

Fix $e\ge2$ and keep all conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
the Cartan datum, the space $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q(q)u_m$
with $u_m=z^av_j$ ($m=j-ae$, $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$), the operators
$K_h,E_i,F_i$, the classical weights $\lambda_j=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$, and the
fixed coproduct $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$,
$\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$,
$\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ of
[[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].
Put $Q:=q^2$ and $c:=Q-1$, and let $Y_j$ denote the operator "multiply the $j$-th
tensor factor by $z$", so that $Y_j$ is invertible with
$Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ in the $j$-th slot and different $Y_j$ commute.

**The affine Hecke algebra $\tilde H_N$.** For $N\ge1$, $\tilde H_N$ is the
unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra with generators $S_1,\dots,S_{N-1}$ and invertible
$Y_1^{\pm1},\dots,Y_N^{\pm1}$ subject to

$$S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q,\qquad S_iS_{i+1}S_i=S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1},\qquad S_iS_j=S_jS_i\quad(|i-j|\ge2),$$

$$Y_iY_j=Y_jY_i,\qquad S_iY_j=Y_jS_i\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}.$$

The element $t_i:=-q^{-1}S_i$ then satisfies $(t_i-q)(t_i+q^{-1})=0$; for a
reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}\in S_N$ put $S_w:=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_k}$
and $A_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ (well defined by the braid relations).

**The two-vector operator and its extension.** On residue tensors
$v_j\otimes v_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$) set

$$S(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}-q\,v_k\otimes v_j,&j<k,\\ -\,v_j\otimes v_j,&j=k,\\ -q\,v_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k,&j>k.\end{cases}$$

For a Laurent monomial $f=Y_1^pY_2^q$ define, with $s(f):=Y_2^pY_1^q$ the
swap of the two loop variables,

$$S(f\,w):=s(f)\,S(w)+(1-Q)\,Y_2\,\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}\,w\qquad(w\in V\otimes V),$$

and extend linearly; the quotient $(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)$ is a Laurent polynomial,
so $S$ is a well-defined linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$.
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ the generator $S_i$ acts by this operator on
the tensor factors $i,i+1$ and $Y_j$ acts on the $j$-th factor as above; this
defines the **affine Hecke action**.

derivations.claim: The first three relations hold in $W_N$. derivations.claim: The cleared identity and normalization. Since $S$ commutes with $a$ and with $Y_1Y_2$, the operator $(a-1)S+q^2-1$ is a Laurent coefficient operator; multiplying by the series $(q^2-a)^{-1}=\sum_{r\ge0}a^rq^{-2r-2}$ gives a well-defined endomorphism of the completion of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ in the $a$-adic direction. Then $R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1=\frac{(a-1)S+q^2-1-(q^2-a)}{q^2-a}=\frac{(a-1)(S+1)}{q^2-a}$, and $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}=1-q^2/a=(a-q^2)/a=-(q^2-a)/a$, so $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=(a^{-1}-1)(S+1)$ exactly in the Laurent domain after clearing. Since $a^{-1}-1\ne0$ and the Laurent ring is a domain, multiplication by $a^{-1}-1$ is injective on the original free Laurent module, so no original vector is lost: $\ker(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=\ker(S+1)$ there.

Symmetries of $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$. By [F1] $S=P\,S_0\,P$ decomposes into the residue swap $P$ and the loop swap $s$ with $S_0$ a residue operator, and $a\mapsto a^{-1}$ under the factor swap; substituting in the definition shows $PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P=(q^2-a^{-1})^{-1}[(a^{-1}-1)P S_0 P+q^2-1]=R_{\mathrm{fix}}$, so $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ swaps the loop variables. On an extremal diagonal $u\otimes u$ the operator $S$ has eigenvalue $-1$ (the $j=k$ case, transported by the loop extension), so the numerator is $(a-1)(-1)+q^2-1=(a-1)(-1)-(a-1)=0$ and $R_{\mathrm{fix}}(u\otimes u)=u\otimes u$; here $a=1$ on the diagonal, so the series is ordinary. Since $S$ commutes with $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$ by [F2] and $a$ has total $d$-degree $0$, $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ commutes with the fixed action.

Yang-Baxter for $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$. Write $R_{\mathrm{fix}}=R_0(a)\,s_{\mathrm{loop}}$ with $R_0(a)=\frac{(a-1)S_0+q^2-1}{q^2-a}$ and $s_{\mathrm{loop}}$ the loop swap, and Baxterize $B_i(x):=(x-1)S_{0,i}+(Q-1)$ with $Q=q^2$ and commuting external scalars $x,y$. In the three-factor window expand $B_1(x)B_2(xy)B_1(y)-B_2(y)B_1(xy)B_2(x)$: reducing $S_{0,i}^2=(Q-1)S_{0,i}+Q$ and the finite braid $S_{0,1}S_{0,2}S_{0,1}=S_{0,2}S_{0,1}S_{0,2}$ of the residue operators turns the difference into the scalar factor $(x-1)(y-1)+(x-1)+(y-1)-(xy-1)=0$ times the identity. The loop permutations supply exactly the arguments $x,y,xy$ on the three factors and the scalar denominators are the common commuting product $(q^2-x)(q^2-xy)(q^2-y)$ after clearing, so the completed operator identity $R_{12}R_{23}R_{12}=R_{23}R_{12}R_{23}$ follows.

The flipped operator. Put $R_{\mathrm{op}}=PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P$ and $\psi_{\mathrm{op}}=1-q^2a$; by [F1] and [F3] the flip exchanges the two tensor factors and the comparison rules, so $R_{\mathrm{op}}$ is the normalized braiding for the opposite coproduct with denominator $\psi_{\mathrm{op}}$, and at $q^0$ the fundamental cases $j>k$, $j=k$, $j<k$ give respectively the loop factors $a,1,1$ before the loop swap; after the swap the leading term is $z^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_1\otimes z^{-H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_2$ with $H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$, which is the energy of the opposite channel.

The opposite kernel and its generators. By step 1.1 and the flip, $\ker(R_{\mathrm{op}}-1)=P\ker(S+1)$. The base kernel elements $v_j\otimes v_j$ and $v_j\otimes v_k-qv_k\otimes v_j$ $(j<k)$ of the two-factor fixed channel give after the flip $v_j\otimes v_j$ and $qv_j\otimes v_k-v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j<k)$; conjugating by loop powers and using the $l=0,\pm1$ Bernstein formulas turns these into the vectors $C_{j,k}=v_j\otimes z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k+qz^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k\otimes v_j$ for $j\ne k$ and $C_{j,j}=v_j\otimes v_j$. The $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-orbit of the extremal diagonal generates all $C_{j,k}$: two consecutive $F$-moves reach every diagonal, one move gives each adjacent $C_{j,k}$, and continuing around the cycle of residues with the $0$-edge loop shift gives every remaining $C$ with its loop power; common loop shifts $Y_1^rY_2^r$ and the symmetric powers $Y_1^n+Y_2^n$ extend the base cases to every gap, and subtracting the leading pair and inducting on the gap as in the straightening recursion proves generation, matching the kernel $N$ of the cited KMPY section with its $C$ generators. Flipping back identifies the fixed-channel quotient with the normal-ordering relations of the finite q-wedge space.

Conclusion. The q-wedge relations of the fixed channel are exactly the kernel of the normalized left braiding $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$: the cleared identity $\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=(a^{-1}-1)(S+1)$ holds in the Laurent domain with injective multiplier $a^{-1}-1$, so the kernels agree before localization; $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ swaps loops, fixes extremal diagonals, intertwines the fixed action and satisfies Yang-Baxter; and its flip is the opposite-channel braiding with energy $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and kernel generated by the $C_{j,k}$.

boundaries.reason: The theorem is stated for each fixed wedge length N at least 1 and the straightening profile is defined on tuples of that length, so no empty wedge enters and there is no empty-case obligation.

boundaries.evidence: The boundary where a correction vanishes is treated: step 2.1's profile records that a leading adjacent swap needs no correction term, and step 2.3's crystal analysis keeps the cases where an arrow is zero separate from the nonzero ones.

The base of the induction is the single leading term: step 1.1 produces coefficients in the Laurent ring whose leading term is the wedge itself, and step 3.1 exhibits the normal wedges as a free generating set with unimodular leading behaviour.

The degenerate adjacent-pair configuration anchors the profile: step 2.1 checks that a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count while a genuine correction strictly decreases dominance of the sorted index multiset, including the alternating pairs relevant at e=2 used in step 2.3.
Indices are kept inside their original bounds: step 2.1 has the multiset of indices fixed under every relation, so after straightening every index lies between the original minimum and maximum.

The basis consists of the explicit normally ordered wedges and the straightening procedure is deterministic, so the basis theorem selects nothing. The Statement's explicit wedges and the deterministic straightening are the whole input.

boundaries.reason: The claims are spanning, independence and a crystal statement, none of them phrased as a biconditional, so the forward axis carries no obligation.
There is no converse direction here: independence and spanning are each proved directly, in steps 2.2 and 1.1 respectively, and no equivalence between them is asserted.

For $N\ge1$ let $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ carry the affine Hecke action and put
$W_N:=V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}\big/\ker A_N$, where $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$;
write $u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}$ for the image of the pure tensor, and let
$\wedge$ denote this product. Call an index tuple **normal** (or normally
ordered) if $m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N$, and set $W_A:=\sum_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\,u_I$,
$W_0:=\bigoplus_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q]\,u_I$, where $u_I$ is the image of
the corresponding ordered wedge.

For $l<m$ write $m-l=ae+b$ with $a\ge0$, $0\le b<e$ (so $a=\lfloor(m-l)/e\rfloor$
and $b$ is the residue difference). The **normal-ordering relations** are:

$$u_l\wedge u_l=0;\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-u_m\wedge u_l\quad(b=0);\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l\quad(a=0,\ b>0);$$

$$u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l-u_{l+ae}\wedge u_{m-ae}-q^{-1}u_{m-ae}\wedge u_{l+ae}\quad(a>0,\ b>0),$$

where the last line is to be read as a relation in $W_N$ and is applied
recursively to its two remaining unordered pairs; each recursion step strictly
decreases the gap of the unordered pair it rewrites and keeps every index
between $l$ and $m$, so the procedure terminates. The energy normal order is
the equivalent formulation through the opposite-channel energy:
$u_{m_1}\wedge u_{m_2}$ is rewritten toward decreasing indices by
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_{m_1}\otimes u_{m_2})>0\iff m_1>m_2$ of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]].

Let $\tilde H_N$ act on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ as in
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]],
put $Q=q^2$, let $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$, and let
$C_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}Q^{l(w)}=\prod_{r=1}^{N}(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})\ne0$.
Then:

(i) $A_N^2=C_NA_N$, and $A_NS_i=S_iA_N=QA_N$ for every $i$; the operator
$P_N:=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear idempotent commuting with
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

(ii) $\ker A_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\ker(S_i+1)$; equivalently, on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$
the kernel of the q-antisymmetrizer is exactly the sum of the two-eigen kernels.

(iii) $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}=\ker A_N\oplus\operatorname{im}A_N$, and the
quotient by $\ker A_N$ is naturally identified with $\operatorname{im}A_N$, on
which $A_N$ acts by the scalar $C_N$. For $N=2$ the kernel $\ker(S_1+1)$ is
spanned by the loop multiples of the partial q-symmetric vectors
$v_j\otimes v_j$ and $v_j\otimes v_k-q\,v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j<k)$, and in the
quotient the three straightening cases of the finite q-wedge definition below hold: the images
of $v_j\otimes v_j$ vanish, and a pair $l<m$ is rewritten as in the three cases
of that definition. At $q=1$ all of this is the ordinary antisymmetrization:
$C_N=N!$ and $\ker A_N$ is the span of the ordinary symmetric tensors.

Let $\tilde H_N$ act on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ as in
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]],
put $Q=q^2$, let $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$, and let
$C_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}Q^{l(w)}=\prod_{r=1}^{N}(1+Q+\cdots+Q^{r-1})\ne0$.
Then:

(i) $A_N^2=C_NA_N$, and $A_NS_i=S_iA_N=QA_N$ for every $i$; the operator
$P_N:=C_N^{-1}A_N$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear idempotent commuting with
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

(ii) $\ker A_N=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\ker(S_i+1)$; equivalently, on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$
the kernel of the q-antisymmetrizer is exactly the sum of the two-eigen kernels.

(iii) $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}=\ker A_N\oplus\operatorname{im}A_N$, and the
quotient by $\ker A_N$ is naturally identified with $\operatorname{im}A_N$, on
which $A_N$ acts by the scalar $C_N$. For $N=2$ the kernel $\ker(S_1+1)$ is
spanned by the loop multiples of the partial q-symmetric vectors
$v_j\otimes v_j$ and $v_j\otimes v_k-q\,v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j<k)$, and in the
quotient the three straightening cases of the finite q-wedge definition below hold: the images
of $v_j\otimes v_j$ vanish, and a pair $l<m$ is rewritten as in the three cases
of that definition. At $q=1$ all of this is the ordinary antisymmetrization:
$C_N=N!$ and $\ker A_N$ is the span of the ordinary symmetric tensors.

Keep the conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]].
Then:

(i) The derived level-$0$ module $V$ has **level-one perfect crystal**
$B=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$ in the sense of axioms (P1)-(P3): the weights of $V$ are
the finite Weyl orbit of $\lambda^\circ=\Lambda_1-\Lambda_0$ in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$
with one-dimensional weight spaces, $B\otimes B$ is connected,
$\varepsilon(b)\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+$ and $\varphi(b)\in P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+$ have
level one for every $b$, the maps $\varepsilon,\varphi:B\to(P_{\mathrm{cl}}^+)_1$
are bijections onto the level-one dominant weights, and
$B_{\min}:=\{b:\langle c,\varepsilon(b)\rangle=1\}$ equals $B$.

(ii) The basis $G(b_j):=v_j$ is a **lower global basis** of $V$ for the ordinary
semilinear bar involution with coefficient bar $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and
$\overline{v_j}=v_j$: the $A_0$-lattice $V_0=\bigoplus_j\mathbb Z[q]v_j$ is
bar-stable up to $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, the images $b_j+G(b_j)\bmod qV_0$ are the
crystal elements, $\bar{E_iv}=E_i\bar v$ and $\bar{F_iv}=F_i\bar v$ for all
$v\in V$, all rank-one strings have exactly two vertices with $E$- and
$F$-coefficients $1$, and the divided powers
$E_i^{(m)},F_i^{(m)}$ vanish for $m\ge2$. Here
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and $A_0=\mathbb Z[q]$ are kept distinct.

(iii) The same statements hold on the affinization with
$G(z^ab_j)=z^av_j$, the loop variable fixed by the bar involution, and the full
$P$-weight $\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}+a\delta$; the finite $V$ is a
$U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-module with $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$-weights and is not a
level-one $P$-graded highest weight module.

On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ put $a=Y_1/Y_2$ and let $P$ be the
flip of the two tensor factors including their loop variables. Define the
completed normalized left operator

$$R_{\mathrm{fix}}:=(q^2-a)^{-1}\bigl[(a-1)S+q^2-1\bigr],\qquad \psi_{\mathrm{fix}}:=1-q^2a^{-1},$$

where $S$ is the two-factor Hecke operator of
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]
and $(q^2-a)^{-1}$ is expanded as the geometric series in $a$ that starts with
$q^{-2}(1+a/q^2+\cdots)$. Then:

(i) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ swaps the two loop variables, fixes every extremal
pure tensor $u\otimes u$, and commutes with the fixed $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action;
the cleared identity
$\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=(a^{-1}-1)(S+1)$ holds in the Laurent
domain, and since multiplication by $a^{-1}-1$ is injective on the original
Laurent-loop module one has $\ker(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=\ker(S+1)$ there, before
any localization.

(ii) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ satisfies the normalized Yang-Baxter equation
$R_{12}R_{23}R_{12}=R_{23}R_{12}R_{23}$ on the three-factor completed module.

(iii) The flipped operator $R_{\mathrm{op}}:=PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P$ with
$\psi_{\mathrm{op}}=1-q^2a$ is the opposite-channel ($\otimes_+$) normalized
braiding of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
its $q^0$-leading term is
$z^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_1\otimes z^{-H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_2$ with the energy
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$, and its kernel is
$N_{\mathrm{op}}=P\ker(S+1)$, the $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-orbit of the extremal
diagonal generated by
$C_{j,k}=v_j\otimes z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k+q\,z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j\ne k)$
and $C_{j,j}=v_j\otimes v_j$. Flipping back gives the fixed-channel quotient
and the normal-ordering relations of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]].

For $N\ge1$ let $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ carry the affine Hecke action and put
$W_N:=V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}\big/\ker A_N$, where $A_N=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$;
write $u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}$ for the image of the pure tensor, and let
$\wedge$ denote this product. Call an index tuple **normal** (or normally
ordered) if $m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N$, and set $W_A:=\sum_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\,u_I$,
$W_0:=\bigoplus_{\text{normal }I}\mathbb Z[q]\,u_I$, where $u_I$ is the image of
the corresponding ordered wedge.

For $l<m$ write $m-l=ae+b$ with $a\ge0$, $0\le b<e$ (so $a=\lfloor(m-l)/e\rfloor$
and $b$ is the residue difference). The **normal-ordering relations** are:

$$u_l\wedge u_l=0;\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-u_m\wedge u_l\quad(b=0);\qquad u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l\quad(a=0,\ b>0);$$

$$u_l\wedge u_m=-q^{-1}u_m\wedge u_l-u_{l+ae}\wedge u_{m-ae}-q^{-1}u_{m-ae}\wedge u_{l+ae}\quad(a>0,\ b>0),$$

where the last line is to be read as a relation in $W_N$ and is applied
recursively to its two remaining unordered pairs; each recursion step strictly
decreases the gap of the unordered pair it rewrites and keeps every index
between $l$ and $m$, so the procedure terminates. The energy normal order is
the equivalent formulation through the opposite-channel energy:
$u_{m_1}\wedge u_{m_2}$ is rewritten toward decreasing indices by
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(u_{m_1}\otimes u_{m_2})>0\iff m_1>m_2$ of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]].

derivations.claim: The normally ordered wedges span $W_N$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$ and $W_A$ over $A$. By [F1] (and [F5] for the loop form) every wedge is a finite $A$-linear combination of normally ordered wedges, and every rewriting step preserves the total index sum and keeps each index between the original minimum and maximum; hence the normal wedges with indices in a fixed finite interval and fixed sum span the corresponding finite-piece quotient. Taking the union over the finitely many indices occurring in the given element gives a finite spanning expression.

The profile terminates. Order the index tuples by the following well-founded data: first the multiset of indices (fixed under every relation), then the dominance order of the sorted tuple (each secondary relation replaces a pair by the more balanced pair $(l+ae,m-ae)$ and its reverse, which strictly increases the lexicographic order of sorted prefix sums as in the classical straightening), and among tuples with equal sorted profile the inversion count (a leading adjacent swap decreases it). Since a strictly decreasing sequence of natural numbers terminates and the sorted multiset can only take finitely many values with fixed sum and interval, the algorithm stops; no bound by the initial inversion count is used, as the mixed cases redistribute the indices.

Field independence. Let $I_1,\dots,I_r$ be finitely many distinct strictly decreasing index tuples and suppose $\sum_kc_ku_{I_k}=0$ in $W_N$ with $c_k\in\mathbb Q(q)$; then $x:=\sum_kc_kt_{I_k}\in\ker A_N$, where $t_{I_k}$ is the raw tensor of $I_k$. Applying $A_N$ gives $\sum_kc_kA_Nt_{I_k}=0$. Specialise the coefficients of the matrix $(A_Nt_{I_k})_k$ at $q=1$: by [F3] $A_N$ becomes the ordinary antisymmetrizer, and $A_Nt_{I_k}$ becomes (a nonzero scalar multiple of) the ordinary antisymmetrisation of the tensor with index multiset $I_k$; these vectors are linearly independent for distinct multisets, so some maximal minor has a nonzero value at $q=1$, hence is a nonzero element of $\mathbb Q(q)$. Therefore $c_1=\cdots=c_r=0$, proving linear independence over the field and, with step 1.1, that the normal wedges are a field basis.

The crystal structure of the ordered wedges. Fix $i$ and a normal integer tuple $I$; the pairs of indices $(i+ke,i+ke+1)$ for the various $k$ are disjoint because $e\ge2$ and their residues alternate, and each pair is either empty, singly occupied or doubly occupied. Empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen under the color-$i$ operators, a singly occupied pair is a two-vertex string with coefficients $1$ by the finite residue rule of [F4], and shifting an index by one either preserves the strict ordering or creates a collision, which is zero by the relation $u_l\wedge u_l=0$. Hence every finite color-$i$ orbit of $I$ is a product of free two-valued bits times frozen pairs, the projected coproduct coefficients are those of the standard tensor product of highest-weight-$1$ strings, and frozen doubly occupied pairs contribute K-weight $0$; by the rank-one tensor rule of [F4] the raw $A_0$-span $W_0$ is stable under the normalized string operators and its residues give a crystal of the affine wedge module.

Integral basis. By step 1.1 the $A$-module $W_A$ is spanned by the normal wedges with Laurent coefficients, and by step 2.2 any finite subfamily is linearly independent over the fraction field, hence over $A\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$; a finitely generated $A$-module spanned by a family that is independent over the fraction field is free on that family (no torsion can occur, and the spanning family is exactly a basis of the localisation). Thus the normal wedges form an $A$-basis of $W_A$, and the chart $W_0$ is the corresponding $\mathbb Z[q]$-span; $W_0$ is not $W_A$ reduced modulo $q$, and the image of the full positive tensor lattice is not identified with $W_0$.

Conclusion. The normally ordered wedges are a $\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A$-basis of $W_A$, the straightening terminates with the stated well-founded profile preserving sums and intervals, and $W_0$ with the residues of the ordered wedges is a crystal basis of the integrable affine wedge module; the positive-lattice and $q=0$ claims are kept separate.

boundaries.evidence: The direct limit is anchored at its extreme cases: step 1.1 stabilizes a finite word by appending a sufficiently deep tail and covers the case where there is nothing to append, and step 1.2 handles the empty partition as the vacuum word.

The q-adic neighbourhoods are the nonzero ideals generated by powers of q in the positive chart, and the zeroth power gives the chart itself: step 2.1 defines the topology by these neighbourhoods and separates it from the full Laurent chart.

The level-one normalization is fixed at the vacuum: the normalized vacuum weight is declared to be Lambda_0 of level one, and step 1.3 computes the recursion of consecutive vacuum weights with the explicit closed formula.

The apparent periodicity of the vacuum weight is a genuine boundary and is denied correctly: step 1.3 verifies the closed formula at the base parameter and records that no shift by the delta period reproduces the vacuum chain, so the degenerate-looking relation is not asserted.

Both ends of the limit are pinned: step 1.1 proves every finite word stabilizes along the appended ground tails, and step 1.2 proves the resulting normal words are exactly the partition-indexed ones, so the finite end and the stable end of the limit are both accounted for.

The limit is taken along the explicit ground tails and the basis is given by an explicit formula in the partition and the charge, so the construction selects nothing from a family. The Definition's explicit ground tails and basis formula carry the construction.

boundaries.reason: The item defines a space, a topology and a family of weights; it asserts no biconditional and therefore owes no forward branch of an equivalence.

No converse statement appears: the alternative description of the limit as a quotient of eventually-vacuum tensors is proved by direct comparison of the two constructions, not claimed as an if-and-only-if with a separate reverse obligation.

citations.quote:
For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]] form a
$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
$A_0$-chart $W_0$ spanned by the normal wedges with $\mathbb Z[q]$ coefficients
is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.

Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to
the residues of $I$. The vector $v_j$ has **classical weight**
$\lambda_j:=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}\in P$ and **residue** $j\in I$.

**Affinization.** The **affinization** $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis $\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$, identified
with $V\otimes\mathbb Q[z,z^{-1}]$ by $u_m:=z^av_j$ whenever
$m=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$; this representation of
$m$ is unique. The operators become

$$K_hu_m:=q^{\langle\lambda_j+a\delta,h\rangle}u_m,\qquad E_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i+1}\,u_{m-1},\qquad F_iu_m:=\delta_{m\equiv i}\,u_{m+1},$$

so that in the $z$-picture
$E_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}z^{a+\delta_{i0}}v_{j-1}$ and
$F_i(z^av_j)=\delta_{j\equiv i}z^{a-\delta_{i0}}v_{j+1}$. We write
$\mathrm{wt}(u_m):=\lambda_j+a\delta\in P$ and $l(u_m):=ae-j=-m$; the
**ordinary order** is $u_m>u_n\iff m>n$.

**Crystal data.** Put $B:=\{b_1,\dots,b_e\}$, $B_{\mathrm{aff}}:=\{u_m\}_{m\in\mathbb Z}$,
and define partial operators $f_i,e_i$ on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by
$f_iu_m:=u_{m+1}$ if $m\equiv i$ and $f_iu_m:=0$ otherwise, and
$e_iu_m:=u_{m-1}$ if $m\equiv i+1$ and $e_iu_m:=0$ otherwise. Let

$$\varepsilon_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i+1},\qquad \varphi_i(u_m):=\delta_{m\equiv i},\qquad \varepsilon(u_m):=\sum_i\varepsilon_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},\qquad \varphi(u_m):=\sum_i\varphi_i(u_m)\Lambda_i^{\mathrm{cl}},$$

in $P_{\mathrm{cl}}$. On the finite set $B$ the same formulas apply through
$b_j\leftrightarrow v_j$, so that $f_ib_j=b_{j+1}$ if $j\equiv i$ and $0$
otherwise, and $e_ib_j=b_{j-1}$ if $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise.

**The opposite channel and its energy.** On $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$
use the tensor rule $\otimes_+$

$$f_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}f_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes f_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}\qquad e_i(x\otimes y):=\begin{cases}e_ix\otimes y,&\varepsilon_i(x)>\varphi_i(y),\\x\otimes e_iy,&\varepsilon_i(x)\le\varphi_i(y),\end{cases}$$

and the **energy function**

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
$M\in\mathbb Z$ the **ground sequence** is $b^\circ_s:=u_{M-s}$ ($s\ge0$).

Fix an integer $e\ge 2$ and put $I:=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z=\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$
with its cyclic order; elements of $I$ are called **residues**. Let
$A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ be the integer matrix with

$$a_{ii}=2,\qquad a_{i,i-1}=a_{i,i+1}=-1\ \ (i\in I)$$

when $e\ge 3$, and with $a_{00}=a_{11}=2$ and the single double edge

let $Q:=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ be the **root lattice**
and $Q^+$ its nonnegative cone, and define the **central element**
$c:=\sum_{i\in I}h_i\in P^{\vee}$. The **level** of $\lambda\in P$ is

involutions $\tau:P\to P$, $P^{\vee}\to P^{\vee}$ with

derivations.claim: Stabilisation of the direct limit. Let a finite word $u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}$ be given and let $m=\min_k i_k$. Choose $N$ with $M-N\le m-r$; then the appended tail $u_{M-r},u_{M-r-1},\dots$ fills the interval $\{M-N,\dots,M-r\}$ completely with consecutive integers, so in any normal term of a straightening step an index that would cross the cutoff collides: after the tail is complete, every further ordered word in that interval with strictly decreasing entries is the ground word itself, and any other term has two equal entries and vanishes. Hence $\varphi_{r,s}$ is independent of $s$ for $s$ large, and the direct limit is the algebraic quotient by the local kernels.

Partition indexing and independence. A normal semi-infinite word has entries $i_1>i_2>\cdots$ eventually equal to the ground tail $M-k+1$ ($k\to\infty$); writing $i_k=\lambda_k-k+1+M$ defines a weakly decreasing sequence of positive parts $\lambda_k$ that is eventually $0$, hence a partition, and conversely every partition gives such a word. The map $\lambda\mapsto|\lambda;M\rangle$ is therefore bijective, and the map is injective because on every finite prefix it factors through the finite normal basis of [F1]; the images span because any element of the direct limit lies in the image of some $\varphi_{r,s}$, whose ordered words index finitely many partitions in that range.

Vacuum weights. The vacuum word is $u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge\cdots$; its weight is $\sum_{k\ge0}\mathrm{wt}(u_{M-k})$ after regularisation. For $M=j-ae$ each step $M-1$ lowers the loop exponent by $\frac1e$, so summing the loop contributions from the phase $j$ to $0$ gives the quadratic shift: if $M=te+r$ with $0\le r<e$, the residues met before reaching $0$ contribute $t$ full cycles and the initial $r$ steps, and adding the finite root part $\lambda$ of the phase gives $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-(\frac{et(t-1)}2+tr)\delta$; the case $M=0$ gives $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ by construction and the recursion $\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$ is the defining property, so the formula is the unique solution. The Cartan $d$-eigenvalue of $|\lambda;M\rangle$ is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of cells with $c-r+M\equiv0$, and the size is the separate grading $|\lambda|$.

The charts and the topology. The three spans of the basis $|\lambda;M\rangle$ are free modules over $A,A_0,\mathbb Z[q]$ respectively, with $F_A\supseteq F_0\supseteq F_{\mathbb Z0}$ and $F_0=\sum_mq^mF_0$; on $F_0$ the sets $q^nF_0$ form a decreasing separated filtration because a nonzero element has a well-defined minimal $q$-valuation, so the induced topology is Hausdorff, and $F_0$ completes to the $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice inside $\mathbb Q((q))$; the full-field completion of an $A_0$-label piece is $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes F_\mu$. The Laurent lattice satisfies $qF_A=F_A$, so the Laurent chart carries no separated $q$-adic topology; the $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes separately to a $\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice.

Conclusion. The charge-$M$ Fock space is the algebraic direct limit of the finite wedge spaces along the ground tails, with a basis indexed by all partitions, the three charts $F_A,F_0,F_{\mathbb Z0}$ are distinct free lattices, the separated topology is induced by $q^nF_0$ (never by $q^nF_A$), and the vacuum weights are $\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-(\frac{et(t-1)}2+tr)\delta$ for $M=te+r$.

For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of

$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
$A_0$-chart $W_0$ spanned by the normal wedges with $\mathbb Z[q]$ coefficients
is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.

[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]]. For $r\le s$ define
the connecting map
$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})
=u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r}\wedge u_{M-r}\wedge u_{M-r-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{M-s+1}$,
so that new entries are the consecutive ground tail
$u_{M-N},u_{M-N-1},\dots$ appended to a prefix of length $N$. The **charge-$M$
Fock space** is the algebraic direct limit $F^{(M)}:=\varinjlim_{N}W_N$ of the
finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write
$|\lambda;M\rangle$ for the image of the normally ordered semi-infinite word
with entries $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ indexed by the positive parts of the
partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to
$u_M\wedge u_{M-1}\wedge u_{M-2}\wedge\cdots$.

The **Laurent, positive and integral charts** of $F^{(M)}$ are

$$F_A:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_0:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}A_0\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad F_{\mathbb Z0}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathbb Z[q]\,|\lambda;M\rangle,\qquad A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}],\ A_0=\mathbb Z[q].$$

The **separated q-adic topology** on the full field space is the one induced by
the filtration $q^nF_0$, never by $q^nF_A=F_A$; a finite $A_0$-label component
completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes
to $\mathbb Q((q))\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}F^{(M)}_\mu$ for the label-weight
pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

**Vacuum weights.** For $M=j-ae$ with $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ and $a\in\mathbb Z$
the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

$$\Omega_M=\Lambda_r-\Bigl(\frac{e\,t(t-1)}{2}+tr\Bigr)\delta.$$

The weight of the partition $\lambda$ is
$\Omega_M-\sum_{\text{cells}}\alpha_{c-r+M}$, its size $|\lambda|$ is a separate
grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.

Fix $e\ge2$ and let $(I,A,D,P,P^\vee,\alpha_i,h_i,\delta,d,c,q)$ be the cyclic
affine type $A$ Cartan datum of
[[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]], so $I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ and
$q_i=q$ for all $i$. Choose once and for all the representatives
$j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$ of the residues of $I$, so that $j=e$ represents the residue
$0$; all indices $j-1$, $j+1$ below are read in this representative range.

**The derived vector module.** Let $V:=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{e}\mathbb Q(q)v_j$ and
define $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$), $E_i$, $F_i$
($i\in I$) on $V$ by

$$K_hv_j:=q^{\langle\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1},h\rangle}v_j,\qquad E_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}\,v_{j-1},\qquad F_iv_j:=\delta_{j\equiv i}\,v_{j+1},$$

where $v_0:=v_e$ and $v_{e+1}:=v_1$ are read cyclically, and $\equiv$ refers to

$$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k):=\chi(j>k)+b-a,\qquad \chi(j>k):=\begin{cases}1,&j>k,\\0,&j\le k,\end{cases}$$

for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$ and $j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$. For a fixed **charge**
$M\in\mathbb Z$ the **ground sequence** is $b^\circ_s:=u_{M-s}$ ($s\ge0$).

On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ put $a=Y_1/Y_2$ and let $P$ be the
flip of the two tensor factors including their loop variables. Define the

$$R_{\mathrm{fix}}:=(q^2-a)^{-1}\bigl[(a-1)S+q^2-1\bigr],\qquad \psi_{\mathrm{fix}}:=1-q^2a^{-1},$$

where $S$ is the two-factor Hecke operator of
[[def-the-affine-hecke-algebra-action-on-finite-tensor-powers-of-the-vector-representation]]
and $(q^2-a)^{-1}$ is expanded as the geometric series in $a$ that starts with
$q^{-2}(1+a/q^2+\cdots)$. Then:

(i) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ swaps the two loop variables, fixes every extremal
pure tensor $u\otimes u$, and commutes with the fixed $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-action;
the cleared identity
$\psi_{\mathrm{fix}}(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=(a^{-1}-1)(S+1)$ holds in the Laurent
domain, and since multiplication by $a^{-1}-1$ is injective on the original
Laurent-loop module one has $\ker(R_{\mathrm{fix}}-1)=\ker(S+1)$ there, before
any localization.

(ii) $R_{\mathrm{fix}}$ satisfies the normalized Yang-Baxter equation
$R_{12}R_{23}R_{12}=R_{23}R_{12}R_{23}$ on the three-factor completed module.

(iii) The flipped operator $R_{\mathrm{op}}:=PR_{\mathrm{fix}}P$ with
$\psi_{\mathrm{op}}=1-q^2a$ is the opposite-channel ($\otimes_+$) normalized
braiding of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
its $q^0$-leading term is
$z^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_1\otimes z^{-H_{\mathrm{op}}}b_2$ with the energy
$H_{\mathrm{op}}(z^ab_j\otimes z^bb_k)=\chi(j>k)+b-a$, and its kernel is
$N_{\mathrm{op}}=P\ker(S+1)$, the $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$-orbit of the extremal
diagonal generated by
$C_{j,k}=v_j\otimes z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k+q\,z^{-\chi(j>k)}v_k\otimes v_j$ $(j\ne k)$
and $C_{j,j}=v_j\otimes v_j$. Flipping back gives the fixed-channel quotient
and the normal-ordering relations of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]].

completes to a $\mathbb Q[\![q]\!]$-lattice, and the full-field component completes

pieces. Separately, the integral $\mathbb Z[q]$-chart completes to a
$\mathbb Z[\![q]\!]$-lattice; this completion is not identified with
$\mathbb Q((q))$ and is not asserted to carry a $\mathbb Q$-vector-space
topology.

the vacuum $P$-weight $\Omega_M$ is normalised by $\Omega_0=\Lambda_0$ and
$\Omega_M-\Omega_{M-1}=\mathrm{wt}(u_M)$; explicitly, if $M=te+r$ with
$0\le r<e$, then

Fix an integer $e\ge 2$ and put $I:=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z=\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$

with the $\mathbb Z$-bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times

derivations.claim: Right-tail vanishing. Write $b=u_m$ and $b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$. If $m\le M-s$ then $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b\otimes b^\circ_s)\le0$ by [F2], and the two indices are already in decreasing order or equal: in the first case the wedge $u_m\wedge u_{M-s}$ is normal with the added index inside the tail; in the second it vanishes by $u_l\wedge u_l=0$. If $H_{\mathrm{op}}\le0$ with $m>M-s$, then $m$ lies strictly inside the interval already filled by the tail, so in any finite prefix containing the tail up to level $m$ the number of available distinct indices below the largest prefix index is exhausted and some normal term has a repeated entry, hence every term of the straightening vanishes; adding more tail entries only adds more collisions. Thus the image in the direct limit is $0$, and the finite prefix statement gives the stated vanishing, with all coefficients in $q^nW_0$ for every $n$ because the element is already $0$.

Left-tail duality. Reverse the order of the index line and apply step 1.1: the mirrored condition with the left tail is the image of the right-tail computation under the order-reversing map $m\mapsto-m$ of the index set, which exchanges the two loop-shift axioms of [F2] and leaves the normal-ordering relations unchanged; hence the dual vanishing holds with the same counting argument.

Deep insertion of a loop-commuting endomorphism. Let $C$ be an endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ with $Cz=zC$ and of nonzero weight. On a fundamental vector $C$ has finitely many terms $u_{m+d}$ with $d$ in a fixed finite set and colors periodic modulo $e$; if $C$ has nonzero weight, no term keeps the index unchanged. Insert $C$ at a slot deep inside a completely filled ground interval of length $r$: every output index stays in the interval, and a strictly decreasing full tuple of $r+1$ distinct integers inside $r$ consecutive integers is impossible, so the resulting wedge is a sum of terms each of which has a collision; hence the insertion is $0$ once the prefix contains the interval. Since deeper insertions only extend the filled interval, the sequence of truncations converges $q$-adically to $0$.

The period operator. The map $T$ prepends $e$ vacuum entries and shifts every old index down by $e$; it preserves the label weight because each shift by $e$ changes the loop exponent by $1$ and the finite phase not at all, and it preserves the size because it moves the partition vector to its image under the period, a bijection on labels of the same size. On the size-$n$ part, applying $T^k$ shifts the old entries down by $ke$ and prepends $ke$ vacuum entries; for $ke>n$ the shape is a partition whose first part is at most $n$ while all its indices have been pushed above the ground cutoff, and the normal basis uniqueness of [F1] leaves no such nonvacuum label, so $T^k=0$. Hence the geometric series is finite on every nonvacuum weight and defines $(1-T)^{-1}$ there.

Finite weight strings. By [F3] a label weight determines $\Omega_M-\text{weight}=\sum_im_i\alpha_i$ and, since the simple roots are independent, the sum $\sum_im_i=|\lambda|$ is determined; there are finitely many partitions of a fixed size, so each label weight has finitely many partition vectors.

Conclusion. Deep insertions into a ground tail vanish exactly by the duplicate/fill argument and give the $q$-adic estimates; loop-commuting nonzero-weight endomorphisms insert to zero sufficiently deep; the period operator has finite geometric inverse on every nonvacuum weight; and each label weight has finitely many vectors, so no unconverted source display is needed.

boundaries.evidence: The vacuum and the empty partition are the base of the bijection: step 1.1 includes the empty partition mapping to the ground word, and the node sums are finite because only boundary corners of the diagram contribute.
Zero terms are treated: steps 2.1 and 2.2 set the contribution to zero exactly on collisions, and step 3.1 computes the diagonal action including the exponent-zero cases.

The single-node instance is the base of both formulas: step 1.1's bijection and the finite-prefix computations of steps 2.1 and 2.2 are read at the smallest nonzero configuration, where exactly one entry shifts.

The degenerate collision case where a node is unavailable is handled: steps 2.1 and 2.2 zero the term when the shifted entry collides with a neighbour, and the wrap of residues is included since colors are read modulo the rank.

For every $N\ge1$ the normally ordered wedges
$\{u_{m_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{m_N}:m_1>m_2>\cdots>m_N\}$ of
[[def-finite-q-wedge-space-and-normal-ordering-relations]] form a
$\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $W_N$ and an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-basis of the
Laurent lattice $W_A$. The straightening algorithm terminates with a
well-founded profile: the total index sum and the ambient index interval are
preserved, secondary pairs become strictly more balanced in the sorted
dominance profile, and a leading adjacent swap decreases the inversion count;
in particular no bound by the initial inversion count alone is used. The
$A_0$-chart $W_0$ spanned by the normal wedges with $\mathbb Z[q]$ coefficients
is a crystal basis: for each color $i$, on the occupied set of a normal tuple
the disjoint pairs $(u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1})$ behave as two-vertex highest-weight
$1$ strings, empty and doubly occupied pairs are frozen, and a shift of an
index by one either stays ordered or collides to zero; hence the residues of
the ordered wedges are stable under the normalized string operators and give a
crystal of the integrable affine wedge module. The image of the full
$\mathbb Z[q]$-tensor lattice need not equal $W_0$, and negative powers of $q$
in the straightening are not asserted to be triangular at $q=0$.

$b^\circ_s=u_{M-s}$ and let $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ be the opposite-channel energy.

the condition $H_{\mathrm{op}}(b\otimes b^\circ_s)\le0$ means that the added
integer index lies inside or below the filled right tail
$\{M-s,M-s-1,\dots\}$; then $b\wedge b^\circ_s=0$, a sufficiently long finite
prefix of the wedge is already $0$, and hence the element lies in $q^nW_0$ for
every $n$.

(ii) **Dual left tail.** The mirrored condition with the left tail gives the
same exact finite vanishing, with the roles of left and right exchanged.

(iii) **Endomorphisms commuting with the loop.** A nonzero-weight endomorphism
$C$ of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ commuting with $z$ has only finitely many
loop-shift/color terms on each fundamental vector; inserting $C$ deep inside a
ground tail is eventually $0$, so it converges $q$-adically to $0$ on every
vector.

(iv) **The period operator.** For the explicit period operator
$T$ on $F^{(M)}$ that prepends $e$ vacuum entries and shifts every old index
down by $e$: $T$ preserves each label-weight/size component, and on the
positive-size-$n$ part its $k$-th power is $0$ as soon as $ke>n$.
Consequently $(1-T)^{-1}=1+T+T^2+\cdots$ is a finite geometric sum on every
nonvacuum weight, and each label weight has only finitely many partition
vectors.

$\varphi_{r,s}(u_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge u_{i_r})

finite wedge spaces along these maps; equivalently it is the quotient of the
eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Write

partition $\lambda$, so that the vacuum $\varnothing$ corresponds to

nodes, a quantity that is $0$ beyond the last column (and for every $j\ge1$ when $\lambda=\varnothing$). Since a partition is weakly

topology.

grading, and the $d$-eigenvalue is $\Omega_M(d)$ minus the number of residue-$0$
cells; no periodicity $\Omega_M=\Omega_{M-e}+\delta$ is asserted.

derivations.claim: The bijection and finiteness of the node sums. The map $\lambda\mapsto(i_k)_{k\ge1}$ with $i_k=M+\lambda_k-k+1$ is a bijection onto normal semi-infinite words because $\lambda$ is weakly decreasing and eventually zero, and $i_k$ is strictly decreasing and eventually equal to the ground tail; a partition of size $n$ has at most $n$ addable and removable nodes, so both sums in the statement are finite.

The $F_i$ formula. On a prefix of length $N$ containing the support of $|\lambda\rangle$, the coproduct action of $F_i$ shifts a selected entry $i_k$ to $i_k+1$, provided $i_k\equiv i$; if $i_k+1=i_{k-1}$ the resulting term has a collision and vanishes by the wedge relations, and otherwise the shift is exactly the addition of the corner cell $(k,\lambda_k+1)$ of residue $i$ by [F3]. The coefficient is the product of the suffix $K$-eigenvalues of the finite coproduct, which is $q^{A_i^r-R_i^r}$: a frozen doubly occupied $i$-pair contributes net weight $0$, and the singly occupied $i$-pairs are exactly the other addable and removable $i$-corners, ordered by content, contributing $+1$ for each addable corner strictly to the right (higher content) of the added node and $-1$ for each removable one.

The $E_i$ formula. For $E_i$ the finite-prefix coproduct shifts an entry with $i_k\equiv i+1$ to $i_k-1$; if it collides the term is zero, and otherwise it deletes the corner cell $(k,\lambda_k)$ of residue $i$, whose smaller diagram is $\mu-\gamma$. The prefix $K$-weight contributes the addable and removable $i$-corners of $\mu-\gamma$ strictly to the left (lower content) of the removed node; the single artificial boundary pair at the cutoff contributes the reciprocal scalar $q^{-\delta_{i\equiv M-N}}$, and appending one more ground entry changes exactly this scalar to its inverse in the same way, so the renormalised operator $q^{-\delta_{i\equiv M-N}}E_i$ is cutoff-independent and defines the stable limit by [F2]. The sign is negative because $E_i$ shifts down in the wedge.

The toral and loop operators. The diagonal action of $K_i$ on a finite prefix is $q^{\#\text{addable}_i-\#\text{removable}_i}$ by the same pairing of residues into occupied and empty pairs, which is $q^{N_i(\lambda)}$; the loop operator shifts all indices by $-e$, which adds one cell to every row and increases the size by $|\lambda|+ \text{const}$ while multiplying by $q^{-1}$ per added cell of residue $0$, so $K_d|\lambda\rangle=q^{-m_0(\lambda)}|\lambda\rangle$ with $m_0$ the number of residue-$0$ cells; for general charge the residue rule is replaced by content $+M$ and $K_d$ by $\Omega_M(d)-m_0$.

Conclusion. Normal wedges are bijective with partitions, and the stable finite-prefix action gives the displayed finite node formulas for $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$ before any relation or crystal statement is invoked.

boundaries.evidence: The empty partition is not an afterthought: step 1.1 includes it as the basis image of the vacuum, and its declared weight reduces to Lambda_0 with nodal data supplied by the same formulas, so the highest-weight case is inside the definition.

The charge-zero chamber is fixed and used: residues are the node content modulo the rank at charge zero, and the loop grading acts by the exponent counting residue-zero cells, so the case of no residue-zero cells is distinguished from the size grading by the definitions and used in step 3.1.

The two extreme families at the level of columns are separated by calibration: regular means every part multiplicity is below the rank and restricted means every adjacent difference is below it, and step 2.1 verifies that the partition with one column of full height is restricted but not regular.

A column of height equal to the rank is the degenerate-looking configuration and is allowed: step 2.1 checks exactly this shape against both conditions, confirming that restricted partitions may contain such columns while regular ones may not.

The regular and restricted ends of the dictionary are both covered: step 1.2 rewrites the adjacent-difference condition into the conjugate's column-height condition over the whole index range, and step 3.1 records the resulting dictionary.

The space, its basis, its residue convention and its operators are all declared by explicit formulas, so nothing is selected from a family. The Definition's declared basis and conventions carry the construction.

derivations.claim: The partition basis and the declared operators. By [F1] the map $\lambda\mapsto|\lambda\rangle$ is a bijection from partitions to normal semi-infinite words and the stable prefix action gives well-defined linear $F_i,E_i,K_i,K_d$; the weights, residues and size grading are read off literally from $i_k=\lambda_k-k+1$, so the Definition introduces no new structure beyond the wedge construction.

The regular/restricted equivalence. For a partition $\lambda$ and $r\ge1$, the number of columns of height exactly $r$ in $\lambda$ is $\lambda'_r-\lambda'_{r+1}$ where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate; evaluating at $r=\lambda_i$ shows that $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}$ is the multiplicity of the column of height $r$ in $\lambda'$, with $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}=0$ exactly when no column of height $r$ exists. Hence $\lambda$ is $e$-restricted (all adjacent differences $<e$) if and only if its conjugate has all part multiplicities $<e$, that is, if and only if $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular; a column of height $e$ is allowed in an $e$-restricted partition because it contributes adjacent difference $e-1<e$.

The boundary example. For $e\ge2$ the partition $(1^e)$ has parts of multiplicity exactly $e$, so it is not $e$-regular, while its adjacent differences are $1,1,\dots,1,1<e$, so it is $e$-restricted; this shows the two conditions are genuinely different and that the full Fock space contains non-regular labels. All partitions are vertices of the full Fock module; the regular ones will be the labels of the empty component.

Conclusion. The level-one partition Fock space is the charge-$0$ Fock space with weight $\Lambda_0-\sum_im_i\alpha_i$ and residues $c-r\bmod e$, its operators are the stable finite-prefix node operators, and the $e$-regular and $e$-restricted conventions are conjugate to each other with the column-height dictionary.

boundaries.evidence: The empty partition is the induction base: step 1.1 computes the count equal to delta on the zero residue and verifies the claimed formula there, so the base of the induction is not the trivial omission it might look like.
